courses.title: Supervised Study
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Assigns problems for independent study incorporating previous instruction and supervised by the instructor.

courses.title: Beginning American Sign Language I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces cultural awareness, comprehension and production skills, and emphasizes basic sentence structure in American Sign Language with a focus on interactive communicative competence. Part I of II. This is a UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Beginning American Sign Language II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4 hours. Total 4 hours per week. Prerequisite: ASL 101 or by placement test.
courses.description: Introduces cultural awareness, comprehension and production skills, and emphasizes basic sentence structure in American Sign Language with a focus on interactive communicative competence. Part II of II. This is a UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Fingerspelling and Number Use in ASL
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours per week. Prerequisite: ASL 101 or permission of instructor.
courses.description: Provides intensive practice in comprehension and production of fingerspelled words and numbers with emphasis on clarity and accuracy. Focuses on lexicalized fingerspelling and numeral incorporation as used by native users of American Sign Language.

courses.title: History of the U.S. Deaf Community
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines the history of the Deaf Community. Presents an overview of various aspects of Deaf culture, including educational and legal issues in American history

courses.title: Intermediate American Sign Language I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: ASL 102 or placement test.
courses.description: Continues to develop cultural awareness, comprehension and production skills, and emphasizes a variety of sentence structures in American Sign Language with a continued focus on interactive communicative competence. Part I of II. This is a UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Intermediate American Sign Language II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: ASL 201 or by placement test
courses.description: Continues to develop cultural awareness, comprehension and production skills, and emphasizes a variety of sentence structures in American Sign Language with a continued focus on interactive communicative competence. Part II of II. This is a UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Comparative Linguistics: ASL and English
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: ASL 102
courses.description: Describes ASL (American Sign Language) and spoken English on five levels: phonological, morphological, lexical, syntactic, and discourse. Compares and contrasts the two languages on all five levels using real-world examples. Documents similarities between signed languages and spoken languages in general. Describes the major linguistic components and processes of ASL and English. Introduces basic theories regarding ASL structure. Emphasizes the status of ASL and English as natural languages by comparing and contrasting similarities and unique differences between the two languages.

courses.title: Advanced American Sign Language I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4 hours. Total 4 hours per week. Prerequisite: ASL 202 or by placement test.
courses.description: Develops cultural awareness, comprehension and production skills, and emphasizes a variety of sentence structures in American Sign Language with a continued focus on advanced communicative competence.

courses.title: Advanced American Sign Language II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4 hours. Total 4 hours per week. Prerequisite: ASL 202 or by placement test.
courses.description: Develops cultural awareness, comprehension and production skills, and emphasizes a variety of sentence structures in American Sign Language with a continued focus on advanced communicative competence.

courses.title: Keyboarding I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-4 hours. Total 2-4 hours per week. A laboratory co-requisite (AST 103) may be required.
courses.description: Teaches the alpha/numeric keyboard with emphasis on correct techniques, speed, and accuracy. Teaches formatting of basic personal and business correspondence, reports and tabulation.

courses.title: Keyboarding II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-4 hours. Total 2-4 hours per week. Prerequisite: AST 101 . A laboratory co-requisite (AST 104) may be required.
courses.description: Develops keyboarding and document production skills with emphasis on preparation of specialized business documents. Continues skill-building for speed and accuracy.

courses.title: Editing/Proofreading Skills
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Develops skills essential to creating and editing business documents. Covers grammar, spelling, diction, punctuation, capitalization, and other usage problems.

courses.title: Keyboarding for Computer Usage
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour per week.
courses.description: Teaches the alphabetic keyboard and 10-key pad. Develops correct keying techniques.

courses.title: Word Processing I (Specify Software)
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour per week.
courses.description: Introduces students to a word processing program to create, edit, save and print documents.

courses.title: Word Processing II (Specify Software)
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour per week.
courses.description: Presents formatting and editing features of a word processing program.

courses.title: Word Processing III (Specify Software)
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour per week.
courses.description: Continues work with formatting features and text enhancements of a word processing program.

courses.title: Records Management
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches filing and records management procedures for hard copy, electronic, and micrographic systems. Identifies equipment, supplies, and solutions to records management problems.

courses.title: Word Processing (Specify Software)
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-4 hours. Total 2-4 hours per week. Prerequisite AST 101 or equivalent. A laboratory co-requisite (AST 144) may be required.
courses.description: Teaches creating and editing documents, including line and page layouts, columns, fonts, search/replace, cut/paste, spell/thesaurus, and advanced editing and formatting features of word processing software.

courses.title: Word Processing II (Specify Software)
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-4 hours. Total 2-4 hours per week. Prerequisite: AST 141 or equivalent. A laboratory co-requisite (AST 145) may be required.
courses.description: Teaches advanced software applications.

courses.title: Introduction to Presentation Software (Spcify Software)
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces presentation options including slides, transparencies, and other forms of presentations.

courses.title: Topics In
courses.contact_hours: May be used also for special honors courses. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Provides an opportunity to explore topical areas of interest to or needed by students.

courses.title: Supervised Study
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Assigns problems for independent study incorporating previous instruction and supervised by the instructor.

courses.title: Microcomputer Office Applications
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-4 hours. Total 2-4 hours per week. Prerequisite: AST 101 or equivalent. A laboratory co-requisite (AST 233) may be required.
courses.description: Teaches production of business documents using word processing, databases, and spreadsheets. Emphasizes document production to meet business and industry standard.

courses.title: Records and Database Management
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-4 hours. Total 2-4 hours per week. A laboratory co-requisite (AST 235) may be required.
courses.description: Teaches filing and records management procedures using microcomputer database software. Incorporates both manual and electronic methods for managing information.

courses.title: Specialized Software Applications (Specify Software)
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-4 hours. Total 2-4 hours per week. Prerequisite: AST 101 or equivalent. A laboratory co-requisite (AST 237) may be required.
courses.description: Teaches specialized integrated software application on the microcomputer. Emphasizes document production to meet business and industry standards.

courses.title: Word Processing Advanced Operations
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-4 hours. Total 2-4 hours per week. A laboratory co-requisite (AST 239) may be required.
courses.description: Teaches advanced word processing features including working with merge files, macros, and graphics; develops competence in the production of complex documents.

courses.title: Office Administration I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: AST 101 .
courses.description: Develops an understanding of the administrative support role and the skills necessary to provide organizational and technical support in a contemporary office setting. Emphasizes the development of critical-thinking, problem-solving, and job performance skills in a business office environment.

courses.title: Office Administration II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: AST 243 or equivalent.
courses.description: Enhances skills necessary to provide organizational and technical support in a contemporary office setting. Emphasizes administrative and supervisory role of the office professional. Includes travel and meeting planning, office budgeting and financial procedures, international issues, and career development.

courses.title: Advanced Desktop Publishing I (Specify Software)
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-4 hours. Total 2-4 hours per week. Prerequisite: AST 101 or equivalent and experience in using a word processing package. A laboratory co-requisite (AST 255) may be required.
courses.description: Introduces specific desktop publishing software. Teaches document layout and design, fonts, type styles, style sheets, and graphics.

courses.title: Coordinated Internship
courses.contact_hours: Credit/practice ratio not to exceed 1:5 hours. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Supervises on-the-job training in selected business, industrial or service firms coordinated by the college.

courses.title: Cooperative Education
courses.contact_hours: Credit/work ratio not to exceed 1:5 hours. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Supervises in on-the-job training for pay in approved business, industrial and service firms, coordinated by the college's cooperative education office. Is applicable to all occupational- technical curricula at the discretion of the college.

courses.title: Supervised Study
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Assigns problems for independent study incorporating previous instruction and supervised by the instructor.

courses.title: Introduction to Automotive Shop Practices
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces shop practices for automotive laboratory and shop safety, identification and use of hand tools, general power equipment and maintenance of automotive shop. Explains basic operation procedures of standard shop equipment. Presents Occupational Safety and Health Act standards pertaining to the automotive field.

courses.title: Introduction to Automotive Systems
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 4-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces fundamental systems of automobile, the engine fuel, exhaust, electric, ignition, lubrication, cooling, transmission, steering, brake and suspension systems. Teaches theory and function of each system. Demonstrates operation.

courses.title: Automotive Engines I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 4-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents analysis of power, cylinder condition, valves and bearings in the automotive engine to establish the present condition, repairs or adjustments. Part I of II.

courses.title: Automotive Engines II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 4-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents analysis of power, cylinder condition, valves and bearings in the automotive engine to establish the present condition, repairs or adjustments. Part II of II.

courses.title: Automotive Fuel Systems I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 0-3 hours. Total 3-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Analyses major domestic and foreign automotive fuel systems to include carburetors and fuel injection systems. Includes detailed inspection and discussion of fuel tanks, connecting lines, instruments, filters, fuel pumps, superchargers, and turbo charger. Also includes complete diagnosis, troubleshooting, overhaul and factory adjustment procedures of all major carbureted and fuel injection systems. Part I of II.

courses.title: Automotive Fuel Systems II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 0-3 hours. Total 3-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Analyses major domestic and foreign automotive fuel systems to include carburetors and fuel injection systems. Includes detailed inspection and discussion of fuel tanks, connecting lines, instruments, filters, fuel pumps, superchargers, and turbo charger. Also includes complete diagnosis, troubleshooting, overhaul and factory adjustment procedures of all major carbureted and fuel injection systems. Part II of II.

courses.title: Anti-Pollution Systems
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies various anti-pollution systems used on modern automobiles, installation, inspection, repair and service.

courses.title: Auto Fuel and Ignition Systems
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-4 hours. Laboratory 3-9 hours. Total 7-11 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies automobile ignition and fuel systems, their functions in operation of engine. Includes carburetors, fuel pumps, ignition systems, troubleshooting, engine test and adjustment, tune-up.

courses.title: Automotive Lubrication and Cooling Systems
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 4-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Analyzes lubrication systems to include lubricants, pumps, lines, filters, and vents. Also analyzes cooling systems, coolants, pumps, fans, lines and connections. Teaches estimating repairs, adjustments needed and their costs.

courses.title: Introduction to Auto Mechanics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 4-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces auto mechanics, covering auto shop safety, tool identification and use. Explains automobile system theory and function. Stresses quality work practices and job opportunities.

courses.title: Automotive Vehicle Inspection
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents information on methods for performing automotive vehicle safety inspection.

courses.title: Auto Power Trains I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2-6 hours. Total 4-8 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents operation, design, construction and repair of power train components, standard and automatic transmission. Includes clutches, propeller shaft, universal joints, rear axle assemblies, fluid couplings, torque converters as well as 2, 3, and 4 speed standard, overdrive and automatic transmissions. Part I of II.

courses.title: Auto Power Trains II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2-6 hours. Total 4-8 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents operation, design, construction and repair of power train components, standard and automatic transmission. Includes clutches, propeller shaft, universal joints, rear axle assemblies, fluid couplings, torque converters as well as 2, 3, and 4 speed standard, overdrive and automatic transmissions. Part II of II.

courses.title: Automotive Diagnostics I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents the application of operating theory and diagnostic procedures on general engine mechanical and electrical systems. Emphasizes diagnostic procedures using the latest diagnostic procedures using the latest diagnostic equipment. Part I of II.

courses.title: Coordinated Internship
courses.contact_hours: Credit/practice ratio not to exceed 1:5 hours. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Supervises on-the-job training in selected business, industrial or service firms coordinated by the college.

courses.title: Cooperative Education
courses.contact_hours: Credit/work ratio not to exceed 1:5 hours. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Supervises in on-the-job training for pay in approved business, industrial and service firms, coordinated by the college's cooperative education office. Is applicable to all occupational- technical curricula at the discretion of the college.

courses.title: Seminar and Project
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Requires completion of a project or research report related to the student's occupational objectives and a study of approaches to the selection and pursuit of career opportunities in the field.

courses.title: Supervised Study
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Assigns problems for independent study incorporating previous instruction and supervised by the instructor.

courses.title: Automotive Systems IV
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents advanced theory and detailed study of automobile systems. Provides laboratory periods for actual field practice in troubleshooting. Part II of II.

courses.title: Emissions Systems Diagnosis and Repair
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents logical diagnostic paths to identify vehicle HC-CO, O2, and NOx failure areas, Teaches a progression of failure detection from most likely to more complex causes. Emphasizes use of infrared analyzer and manufacturer's specified adjustments.

courses.title: High Efficiency Fuel Systems
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 7 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents a study of high efficiency fuel systems and related emission control systems.

courses.title: Computerized Fuel Systems
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Laboratory 3-6 hours. Total 5-7 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces devices which sense the engine condition and control fuel mixture to produce economical fuel consumption. Teaches theory of operation, testing, adjustment and repair or replacement of these devices.

courses.title: Advanced ASM Emissions Diagnostics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents logical diagnostic strategies to identify and correct vehicle HC, CO, and Nox emissions failures. Specifically addresses the technologies and techniques required for successful diagnosis and repair of vehicles failing Acceleration Simulation Mode (ASM) and Two-Speed Idle Mode Tests. Current ASM diagnostic equipment will be introduced, discussed, and usage demonstrated.

courses.title: Hybrid Electric Vehicle Technology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 4-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents technologies used in hybrid electrical vehicles (HEV), includes safety, theory, diagnosis, and component replacement. Covers automotive electronics; theory, operation and testing.

courses.title: Automotive Heating and Air Conditioning
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 3-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies separate and combined automotive heaters and air conditioning, including direct and vacuum operated controls, basic principles of refrigeration, adjustment, general servicing, and charging of air conditioning systems.

courses.title: Automotive Climate Control
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces principles of refrigeration, air conditioning controls, and adjustment and general servicing of automotive air conditioning systems.

courses.title: Automotive Accessories
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-3 hours. Laboratory 0-3 hours. Total 2-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the principles, design, construction, adjustment, and maintenance of all automotive equipment classed as an accessory which is not studied in other automotive courses.

courses.title: Automotive Electricity I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 4-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces electricity and magnetism, symbols and circuitry as applied to the alternators, regulators, starters, lighting systems, instruments and gauges and accessories. Part I of II.

courses.title: Automotive Electricity II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 4-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces electricity and magnetism, symbols and circuitry as applied to the alternators, regulators, starters, lighting systems, instruments and gauges and accessories. Part II of II.

courses.title: Automotive Electronics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 0-3 hours. Total 3-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces field of electronics as it applies to the modern automobile. Emphasizes basic circuit operation, diagnosis and repair of digital indicator and warning systems.

courses.title: Automatic Transmissions
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2-6 hours. Total 4-8 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies several types of automatic transmissions, torque converters, and their principles of operation. Includes adjustment, maintenance, and rebuilding.

courses.title: Automotive Drivetrains
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 6 hours. Total 8 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents the operation, design, diagnosis, and repair of manual, automatic transmissions, and final drive systems, for both front and rear drive vehicles. Covers clutches, synchronizers, torque converters, differentials, drive axles, U-joints, CV joints, 4-wheel drive, and all-wheel drive systems.

courses.title: Advanced Automotive Engine Performance Diagnostics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 6 hours. Total 8 hours per week. Prerequisite: AUT 155 .
courses.description: Introduces advanced engine performance concepts, including theory and practical application. Covers vehicle communications, scan-tool diagnostics, advanced engine mechanical tests, and diagnosing and repairing complex vehicle drivability issues. Provides preparation for the Automotive Service Excellence (ASE) A8 Engine Performance Certification examination.

courses.title: Automotive Braking Systems
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents operation, design, construction, repair, and servicing of braking system, including Anti-Lock Brake Systems (ABS). Explains uses of tools and test equipment, evaluation of test results, estimation of repair cost for power, standard and disc brakes.

courses.title: Auto Alignment, Suspension and Steering
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Laboratory 6 hours. Total 7-8 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces use of alignment equipment in diagnosing, adjusting, and repairing front and rear suspensions. Deals with repair and servicing of power and standard steering systems.

courses.title: Automotive Suspension and Braking Systems
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 4-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents the operation, design, construction, repair and servicing of braking and suspension systems. Explains use of tools and test equipment, evaluation of test results, estimation and repair cost, front and rear suspension alignment, power and standard steering, and power, standard and disc brakes.

courses.title: Automotive Driveability and Tune-Up I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents diagnostic and service procedures for automatic electrical and mechanical systems. Teaches use of tools and test equipment, evaluation of test results, estimation of repair cost. Emphasizes performance of required service. Part I of II.

courses.title: Shop Management
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies shop layout, personnel management, cost analysis, record keeping and quality control. Discusses shop manager, service salesman, and service writer's roles in customer relations.

courses.title: Coordinated Internship
courses.contact_hours: Credit/practice ratio not to exceed 1:5 hours. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.

courses.title: General Biology I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Recitation and laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on biological processes with a chemical foundation, including macromolecules, cellular structure, metabolism, and genetics in an evolutionary context. Explores the core concepts of evolution; structure and function; information flow, storage and exchange; pathways and transformations of energy and matter; and systems biology. Emphasizes the process of science, interdisciplinary approach, and relevance of biology to society. Part I of a two-course sequence. Assignments require college-level reading fluency, coherent written communication, and basic mathematical skills. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course. Credit toward graduation cannot be awarded for both BIO 101 and BIO 106 .

courses.title: General Biology II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Recitation and laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week. Prerequisite: BIO 101 or Departmental Permission
courses.description: Focuses on biological processes with a chemical foundation, including macromolecules, cellular structure, metabolism, and genetics in an evolutionary context. Explores the core concepts of evolution; structure and function; information flow, storage and exchange; pathways and transformations of energy and matter; and systems biology. Emphasizes the process of science, interdisciplinary approach, and relevance of biology to society. Part II of a two-course sequence. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: General Botany
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Recitation and laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Emphasizes plant life cycles, anatomy, morphology, taxonomy, and evolution. Considers the principles of genetics, ecology, and physiology.

courses.title: General Zoology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Recitation and laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents basic biological principles, and emphasizes structure, physiology and evolutionary relationships of invertebrates and vertebrates.

courses.title: Human Anatomy and Physiology I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week. Corequisite or Prerequisite: Demonstration of NAS 2 concepts of Chemical Concepts, Cytology, and Inheritance through NAS 2 completion; or assessment; or module completion; or equivalent.
courses.description: Presents the study of anatomy & physiology including anatomical terminology, homeostasis, histology, integumentary system, skeletal system, muscular system, and nervous system. Part I of II. Assignments require college-level reading fluency, coherent written communication, and basic mathematical skills.

courses.title: Human Anatomy and Physiology II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week. Prerequisite: Completion of BIO 141 with a grade of C or better.
courses.description: Continues study of anatomy and physiology including endocrine system, blood and cardiovascular system, lymphatic system and immunity, respiratory system, urinary system, fluid, electrolyte, and acid-base balance, digestive system and nutrient metabolism, reproductive system, and prenatal development. Part II of II.

courses.title: Basic Human Anatomy and Physiology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Surveys human anatomy and physiology. Covers basic chemical concepts, cellular physiology, anatomy, and physiology of human organ systems. Assignments require college-level reading fluency, coherent written communication, and basic mathematical skills.

courses.title: Human Heredity
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Surveys basic principles of classical and molecular genetics as applied to humans.

courses.title: Microbiology for Health Science
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Recitation and laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week. Prerequisite: BIO 101 or BIO 141
courses.description: Focuses on the general characteristics, cellular structure, and metabolism of microorganisms. Emphasizes microbial relationships with individual and community health. Includes impact of microbes on human health and disease, microbial pathogenicity, identifying and managing infectious diseases and controlling microbial growth, healthcare associated infections and epidemiology. Studies aseptic culturing techniques with hands-on experience in safe microbiology practices.

courses.title: Principles in Regulatory and Quality Environments for Biotechnology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Total 2 hours per week. Pre- or co-requisite: BIO 180 .
courses.description: Prepares students to work effectively in a scientific field and explains the basics of the regulatory and quality environments encountered in a biotechnology or pharmaceutical field. Surveys the principles and practices used on a day-to-day basis in regulatory affairs and quality systems.

courses.title: Biotechnology Methods
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides students with laboratory skills needed for employment in the biotechnology industry. Focuses on widely used biotechnology procedures in areas of DNA analysis, protein analysis, tissue culture, monoclonal antibodies quality control assays and diagnostic procedures.

courses.title: Introduction to Careers in Biotechnology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours per week.
courses.description: Exposes the student to the field of biotechnology including skills, opportunities, and employment opportunities. Introduces the requirements to complete training and facilitates the student's need in the construction of a student plan and educational goal.

courses.title: General Microbiology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Recitation and laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week. Prerequisites: ENG 111 , BIO 101 , BIO 102 , and CHM 111 Corequisite: CHM 112
courses.description: Explores the structure and function of microorganisms and their relationship to the environment and humans. Emphasizes the various groups of microorganisms, their growth and metabolism, roles in the functioning of ecosystems, genetics, their roles in human health, the use of microbes in industrial applications and biotechnology and methods of microbial control.

courses.title: Cell Biology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Recitation and Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week. Prerequisites: BIO 101 and CHM 111 .
courses.description: Introduces the ultrastructure and functions of cells. Emphasizes cell metabolism, cell division, and control of gene expression.

courses.title: Plant Life of Virginia
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Recitation and laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on identification and ecological relationships of the native plants of Virginia. Emphasizes the natural communities of trees, shrubs, herbaceous plants, ferns, and some invasive species.

courses.title: Immunology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisites: BIO 101 or equivalent and BIO 150 or equivalent.
courses.description: Provides an introduction to immune organs and tissues as well as a more in-depth analysis of immune function at the cellular and molecular level. Combines concepts of cell biology, genetics, developmental biology and biochemistry. Applies learned material to clinical applications and human health, including how the immune system can be manipulated and how failures of the immune response may lead to human disease.

courses.title: Human Anatomy and Physiology I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week. Prerequisites: BIO 101 , BIO 102 , CHM 111 , and CHM 112
courses.description: Integrates the study of gross and microscopic human anatomy with physiology, emphasizing the analysis and interpretation of physiological parameters, as they relate to clinical scenarios. Covers the integumentary system, skeletal system (including articulations), muscular system, and nervous system. Part I of II.

courses.title: Human Anatomy and Physiology II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week. Prerequisites: Completion of BIO 231 with a grade of C or better.
courses.description: Integrates the study of gross and microscopic human anatomy with physiology, emphasizing the analysis and interpretation of physiological parameters, as they relate to clinical scenarios. Covers the endocrine system, circulatory system, lymphatic system (including immunity), respiratory system, urinary system (including fluid, electrolyte, and acid-base balance), digestive system (including nutrient metabolism), and reproductive system (including prenatal development). Part II of II.

courses.title: Biotechnology Concepts
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisites: BIO 101 or BIO 173 , or instructor permission.
courses.description: Explores the growing field of biotechnology ranging from basic cellular and molecular biology concepts to both basic and advanced laboratory techniques. Emphasizes the application of biotechnology to medicine, agriculture, environmental science, and forensics. Includes discussion of the business, regulatory/legal, ethical, and societal issues of this topic as well as the growing field of bioinformatics.

courses.title: Bioinformatics and Computer Applications in Biotechnology
courses.contact_hours: (2 Cr.) Lecture 2 hours. Total 2 hours per week. Local
courses.description: Covers basic computer concepts and Internet skills and uses a software suite, which includes word processing, spreadsheet, database, and presentation software to demonstrate skills as they are applied to biotechnology. Introduces students to basic online tools and resources to retrieve and analyze biological data, such as DNA, RNA, and protein sequences, structures, functions, pathways, and interactions. Includes hands-on sessions to allow students to become familiar with these resources and their navigation and applications.

courses.title: General Genetics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Recitation and laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week. Prerequisites: BIO 101 & BIO 102 or equivalent.
courses.description: Explores the principles of genetics ranging from classical Mendelian inheritance to the most recent advances in the biochemical nature and function of the gene. Includes experimental design and statistical analysis.

courses.title: General Ecology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Recitation and laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week. Prerequisites: BIO 101 and BIO 102 .
courses.description: Studies interrelationships between organisms and their natural and cultural environments with emphasis on populations, communities, and ecosystems.

courses.title: Coastal Ecology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Investigates beach, saltmarsh, and estuarine ecosystems including the effects of chemical, geological, and physical factors upon the distribution of organisms. Discusses the effects of pollution and human manipulation of the coastline. Includes observation and identification of coastal plants and animals, and analysis of the dynamics of coastal community structure and function in a field-based setting.

courses.title: Biological Problems in Contemporary Society
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Discusses major biological problems facing society which may include environmental and health concerns such as pollution, bioengineering, drug abuse, conservation, famine and others.

courses.title: Construction Management I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents overviews of all phases of construction project management. Introduces students to philosophy, responsibilities, methodology, and techniques of the construction process. Introduces topics related to the construction and design industries, organizations, construction contracts, bidding procedures, insurance, taxes, bonding, cost accounting, business methods, including basic computer usage, safety and general project management procedures.

courses.title: Construction Management II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Emphasizes advanced management techniques and methodology. Includes engineering economics, accounting principles, life cycle costing, value engineering, systems analysis with computer applications, work improvement, quality control, and a broad overview of the construction management profession.

courses.title: Principles of Residential Building Construction Inspect
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces general principles of residential building inspection including materials, foundations, framing, finishing, and building codes. Use local pre/co-requisites.

courses.title: Shop Practices and Procedures
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 3-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces basic hand and power tools with emphasis on proper care and safety practices. Introduces materials used in building trades including metals, plastics, and woods with stress placed on the processing techniques of each. Emphasizes fasteners such as screws, rivets, and glues as well as brazed, soldered, and welded joints.

courses.title: Introduction to Construction
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Covers basic knowledge and requirements needed in the construction trades. Introduces use of tools and equipment, with emphasis on construction safety, including personal and tool safety. Provides a working introduction to basic blueprint reading and fundamentals of construction mathematics.

courses.title: Blueprint Reading and the Building Code
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours.Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces reading and interpreting various kinds of blueprints and working drawings with reference to local, state, and national building codes.

courses.title: Building Codes
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines the building codes and standards applicable to building construction and inspection processes. Covers how to search, interpret and implement the Virginia Uniform State Wide Building Code.

courses.title: Green Building Practices
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Total 1 hour per week.
courses.description: Introduces techniques that reduce the environmental impact of building construction and operation. Uses the analysis of the Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design (LEED) green building rating system.

courses.title: Introduction to Carpentry Trades
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: BLD 110 .
courses.description: Introduces entry-level students to the carpentry trade(s), the Wheels of Learning apprenticeship programs, various types of fasteners, and the wide variety of building materials.

courses.title: Basic Carpentry Principles
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: BLD 125 .
courses.description: Introduces students to basic floor and wall construction.

courses.title: Carpentry Framing I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 4 hours. Total 7 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents an introduction to carpentry with emphasis on residential construction. Covers safety on the job, appropriate use of power tools, basic construction techniques, an introduction to working drawings, and the team approach to residential buildings. Presents an introduction to selection and use of ladders and scaffolds, basic form removal and demolition, and use of basic first aid. Includes the concepts of carpentry framing for floors, walls, ceilings, porches and decks. Includes theoretical and practical application as well as the concepts of carpentry framing for roof, truss installation and door and window installation. Part I of II.

courses.title: Carpentry Framing II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 4 hours. Total 7 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents an introduction to carpentry with emphasis on residential construction. Covers safety on the job, appropriate use of power tools, basic construction techniques, an introduction to working drawings, and the team approach to residential buildings. Presents an introduction to selection and use of ladders and scaffolds, basic form removal and demolition, and use of basic first aid. Includes the concepts of carpentry framing for floors, walls, ceilings, porches and decks. Includes theoretical and practical application as well as the concepts of carpentry framing for roof, truss installation and door and window installation. Part II of II.

courses.title: Building Construction Carpentry
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents woodworking technologies in carpentry. Introduces types of framing and building materials and equipment used in residential and light commercial construction. Emphasizes the development of skills in the safe use of hand and machine woodworking tools and development of construction terminology. Includes laboratory involvement in wall framing and carpentry practices.

courses.title: Construction Field Operations
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces areas of construction field management which relate directly to on-the-job requirements of construction operations viewed from the construction superintendent's standpoint. Includes theories of project management and field supervision; utilization of equipment, labor and material; construction site development; requirements of field scheduling; management input requirements; job recording and documentation; supervision responsibility.

courses.title: Building Structures
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces analysis and design of steel, wood, and reinforced concrete structural members including loads, reactions, bending moments, stresses, and deflection for selection of beam and column sizes. Considers bolted and welded connections in steel design. Introduces determination of reinforcing steel sizes and arrangements in concrete embers. Use local prerequisites.

courses.title: Construction Estimating I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on materials take-off and computing quantities from working drawings and specifications. Includes methods for computing quantities of concrete, steel, masonry, roofing, excavation. Deals with pricing building components, materials and processes, as well as transportation and handling costs, mark-up discount procedures, equipment cost and labor rates.

courses.title: Construction Estimating II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents an introduction to computer programs for construction estimating. Produces a cost estimate for a major project with the aid of a computer program. Use local prerequisites.

courses.title: Construction Management III
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents fundamentals of construction supervision including responsibilities of the construction superintendent, operations manager, general superintendent and project engineer, with factors relating to their work and that of their subordinates, aspects of job leadership and effective human relations as related to efficient supervision.

courses.title: Construction Management IV
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents a comprehensive overview of all aspects of construction law and labor relation, exposing the students to responsibilities and requirements. Includes history of labor relations in the United States, trade unionism, federal labor laws and their direct effect on construction, OSHA (Occupational Safety and Health Act) laws and regulations that apply.

courses.title: Construction Planning and Scheduling
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces principles of planning and scheduling of a construction project. Includes sequence of events and processes on a construction site. Studies scheduling techniques including the critical path method.

courses.title: Seminar and Project
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Requires completion of a project or research report related to the student's occupational objectives and a study of approaches to the selection and pursuit of career opportunities in the field.

courses.title: Supervised Study
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Assigns problems for independent study incorporating previous instruction and supervised by the instructor.

courses.title: Introduction to Business
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Exposes students to the functions and topics of modern business, including economics, management, finance, accounting, marketing, production, international business, small business, and other areas of general business interest. Guides students in establishing a viable business vocabulary, fostering critical and analytical thinking, and refining business decision-making skills.

courses.title: Principles of Supervision I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches the fundamentals of supervision, including the primary responsibilities of the supervisor. Introduces factors relating to the work of supervisor and subordinates. Covers aspects of leadership, job management, work improvement, training and orientation, performance evaluation, and effective employee/ supervisor relationships.

courses.title: Principles of Supervision II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week. Prerequisite: BUS 111 .
courses.description: Develops skills in carrying out the responsibilities of a supervisor including interviewing, evaluating and disciplining, and problem-solving techniques.

courses.title: Entrepreneurship
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents the various steps considered necessary when going into business. Includes areas such as product-service analysis, market research evaluation, setting up books, ways to finance startup, operations of the business, development of business plans, buyouts versus starting from scratch, and franchising. Uses problems and cases to demonstrate implementation of these techniques. This course applies to career/technical education (CTE) programs.

courses.title: Leadership Development
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Covers interpersonal relations in hierarchical structures. Examines the dynamics of teamwork, motivation, handling change and conflict and how to achieve positive results through others.

courses.title: Concepts of Supervision
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches the five functions of management: planning, organizing, staffing, directing and controlling. Includes instruction in leadership skills, problem-solving and decision-making, effective communications, dealing with conflict and employee relations, time management, delegation, and motivation.

courses.title: Business Mathematics I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Applies mathematical operations to business processes and problems. Reviews operations, equations, percents, sales and property taxes, insurance, checkbook and cash records, wage and payroll computations, depreciation, overhead, inventory turnover and valuation, financial statements, ratio analysis, commercial discounts, markup, and markdown.

courses.title: Business Mathematics II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Applies mathematical operations to business processes and problems. Reviews basic statistics, distribution of profit and loss in partnerships, distribution of corporate dividends, simple interest, present value, bank discount notes, multiple payment plans, compound interest, annuities, sinking funds, and amortization.

courses.title: Applied Business Mathematics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Applies mathematical operations to business process and problems such as wages and payroll, sales and property taxes, checkbook records and bank reconciliation, depreciation, overhead, distribution of profit and loss in partnerships, distribution of corporate dividends, commercial discounts, markup, markdown, simple interest, present values, bank discount notes, multiple payment plans, compound interest annuities, sinking funds, and amortization.

courses.title: Introduction to Business Information Systems
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides an overview of business information systems. Introduces computer hardware, software, procedures, systems, and human resources, and explores their integration and application in business. Discusses fundamentals and applications of computer problem-solving and programming.

courses.title: Small Business Management
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Identifies management concerns unique to small businesses. Introduces the requirements necessary to initiate a small business, and identifies the elements comprising a business plan. Presents information establishing financial and administrative controls, developing a marketing strategy, managing business operations, and the legal and government relationships specific to small businesses.

courses.title: Financial Management for Nonprofit Organizations
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents strategies to develop and sustain fiscal responsibility throughout a nonprofit organization, including the understanding of roles and responsibilities of the board of directors, and management and staff. Examines the unique position of nonprofit organizations and their complex interrelationships with both the public and private sectors.

courses.title: Coordinated Internship
courses.contact_hours: Credit/practice ratio not to exceed 1:5 hours. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Supervises on-the-job training in selected business, industrial or service firms coordinated by the college.

courses.title: Supervised Study
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Assigns problems for independent study incorporating previous instruction and supervised by the instructor.

courses.title: Principles of Management
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches management and the management functions of planning, organizing, leading, and controlling. Focuses on application of management principles to realistic situations managers encounter as they attempt to achieve organizational objectives.

courses.title: Organizational Behavior
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents a behaviorally oriented course combining the functions of management with the psychology of leading and managing people. Focuses on the effective use of human resources through understanding human motivation and behavior patterns, conflict management and resolution, group functioning and process, the psychology of decision-making, and the importance of recognizing and managing change.

courses.title: Project Management
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides students with knowledge of essential skills and techniques necessary to lead or participate in projects assigned to managerial personnel. Covers time and task scheduling, resource management, problem solving strategies and other areas related to managing a project.

courses.title: Human Resource Management
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces employment, selection, and placement of personnel, forecasting, job analysis, job descriptions, training methods and programs, employee evaluation systems, compensation, benefits, and labor relations.

courses.title: Advanced Project Management
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours. Total 3-4 hours per week. Prerequisite: BUS 204 .
courses.description: Provides students with in-depth knowledge and advanced skills and techniques necessary to lead projects assigned to project managers. Covers project initiating, project planning, project executing, project monitoring and controlling, and project closing.

courses.title: Continuous Quality Improvement
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents the different philosophies in Quality Control. Introduces students to Process Improvement, Team Development, Consensus Building, and Problem-Solving strategies. Identifies methods for Process Improvement in manufacturing and service organizations which includes Statistical Process Control when used in the quality control function of business and industry.

courses.title: Purchasing and Materials Management
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches the principles of effective purchasing and management of materials and equipment. Includes determination of requirements, source selection, pricing, value analysis, contracting, inventory management, and equipment requisition decisions.

courses.title: Probability and Statistics for Business and Economics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces methods of probability assessment and statistical inference. Includes data collection and presentation; descriptive statistics; basic probability concepts; discrete and continuous probability distributions; decision theory; sampling and estimation; and hypothesis testing. Emphasizes business and economic applications. Utilizes computer software as a tool for problem solving.

courses.title: Business Statistics I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: MTH 161 or division approval.
courses.description: Focuses on statistical methodology in the collection, organization, presentation, and analysis of data; concentrates on measures of central tendency, dispersion, probability concepts and distribution, sampling, statistical estimation, normal and T distribution and hypotheses for means and proportions.

courses.title: Business Statistics II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: BUS 221 or division approval.
courses.description: Continues study of inferential statistics and application of statistical techniques and methodology in business. Includes analysis of variance, regression and correlation measurement of business and economic activity through the use of index numbers, trend, cyclical, and seasonal effects and the Chi-Square distribution and other non-parametric techniques.

courses.title: Business Statistics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: MTH 161
courses.description: Introduces methods of probability assessment and statistical inference. Includes data presentation; descriptive statistics; basic probability concepts; discrete and continuous probability distributions; decision theory; estimation and sampling distributions; Central Limit Theorem; simple linear regression and hypothesis testing for a single sample or population. Emphasizes business and economic applications. Utilizes spreadsheet software as a tool for problem-solving.

courses.title: Applied Business Statistics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces statistics as a tool in decision making. Emphasizes ability to collect, present, and analyze data. Employs measures of central tendency and dispersion, statistical inference, index number, and time series analysis.

courses.title: Computer Business Applications
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week. Prerequisite: keyboarding competence.
courses.description: Provides a practical application of software packages, including spreadsheets, word processing, database management, and presentation graphics. Includes the use of programs in accounting techniques, word processing, and management science application.

courses.title: Business Analytics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: BUS 224 or MTH 245 .
courses.description: Includes overview of quantitative methods in business decision-making, simple and multiple regression and correlation analysis, time series analysis and business forecasting, decision analysis, linear programming, transportation and assignment methods, and network models. May include computer applications. Students will be required to use computer applications.

courses.title: Business Letter Writing
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Applies composition principles to business correspondence, employment documents, and reports (including presentation of data in various chart formats). Focuses on preparing effective communications with customers, suppliers, employees, the public, and other business contacts.

courses.title: Communication in Management
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the functions of communication in management with emphasis on gathering, organizing, and transmitting facts and ideas. Teaches the basic techniques of effective oral and written communication.

courses.title: Introduction to Business Law
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides an introduction to the American legal system and the use of law to achieve economic and social goals. Highlights ethical principles and legal reasoning underlying the rights and obligations of business relationships and their effect on business decision-making. Emphasizes fundamental principles of government regulation and the court system, constitutional law, torts, criminal law, contracts, agency, employment, and property law.

courses.title: Business Law I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Develops a basic understanding of the US business legal environment. Introduces property and contract law, agency and partnership liability, and government regulatory law. Students will be able to apply these legal principles to landlord/tenant disputes, consumer rights issues, employment relationships, and other business transactions.

courses.title: Business Law II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on business organization and dissolution, bankruptcy and Uniform Commercial Code. Introduces international law and the emerging fields of E-Commerce and Internet Law.

courses.title: Inventory and Warehouse Management
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Emphasizes the relationships of inventory and warehouse management to customer service and profitability of the wholesale distributor. Focuses on the role of computerized systems and resulting information for effective management of inventory and the warehouse under various conditions.

courses.title: Ethical Issues in Management
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines the legal, ethical, and social responsibilities of management. May use cases to develop the ability to think and act responsibly.

courses.title: Interpersonal Dynamics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on intra- and interpersonal communication effectiveness in the business organization. Includes topics such as planning and running effective meetings, networking and politicking, coaching and mentoring, making effectual and ethical decisions, developing team-building strategies, and practicing proficient skills in verbal, non-verbal, and written communications.

courses.title: Foundations of Entrepreneurship
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces students to the principles of entrepreneurship, covering business models, responsibilities, and successful practices. BUS 274 serves both transfer and CTE programs.

courses.title: Introduction to International Business
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: BUS 100 or departmental approval
courses.description: Provides an introduction to the theoretical principles and practices of the global business environment. Examines the functions of international business in the economy, international and transnational marketing, production, and financial operations.

courses.title: Technical Drafting I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Laboratory 2-6 hours. Total 3-7 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces technical drafting from the fundamentals through advanced drafting practices. Teaches lettering, metric construction, technical sketching, orthographic projection, sections, intersections, development, fasteners, theory and applications of dimensioning and tolerances. Includes pictorial drawing, and preparation of working and detailed drawings. Part I of II. (Credit will not be awarded for both CAD 111 and DRF 111 .)

courses.title: Introduction to Graphic Representation
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 4-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches use of instruments, lettering, sketching, and drawing conventions. Emphasizes legible drawings and the value of presentation. (Credit will not be awarded for both CAD 120 and DRF 120 .)

courses.title: Introduction to Geometric Dimensions and Tolerancing
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour per week.
courses.description: Presents an overview of a positional tolerance system, its relationship to coordinate tolerance systems, and other aspects of industry standard drafting practices. (Credit will not be awarded for both CAD 127 and DRF 127 .)

courses.title: Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches use of a positional tolerance system, its relationship to coordinate tolerance systems, and other aspects of industry standard drafting practices. (Credit will not be awarded for both CAD 128 and DRF 128 .)

courses.title: Electrical/Electronic Blueprint Reading
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents an interpretation of basic shop drawings, conventional symbols, terminology, and principles used by the mechanical draftsman. Explains common electrical and electronic symbols, wiring diagrams, schematic drawing, and application of wiring diagrams, schematic drawings, and application of wiring diagrams. (Credit will not be awarded for both CAD 135 and DRF 135 .)

courses.title: Technical Drawing
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Enhances the principles learned that are related directly to the field of drafting and design. Gives a more in-depth exposure to detail and working drawings, dimensioning, tolerancing and conventional drafting practices. Teaches CAD modeling, may include parametric modeling. (Credit will not be awarded for both CAD 140 and DRF 140 .)

courses.title: Engineering Drawing Fundamentals I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Laboratory 4-6 hours. Total 5-7 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces technical drafting from the fundamentals through advanced drafting practices. Includes lettering, geometric construction, technical sketching, orthographic projection, sections, intersections, development, fasteners. Teaches theory and application of dimensioning and tolerances, pictorial drawing, and preparation of drawings. Part I of II. (Credit will not be awarded for both CAD 151 and DRF 151 .)

courses.title: Engineering Drawing Fundamentals II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Laboratory 4-6 hours. Total 5-7 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces technical drafting from the fundamentals through advanced drafting practices. Includes lettering, geometric construction, technical sketching, orthographic projection, sections, intersections, development, fasteners. Teaches theory and application of dimensioning and tolerances, pictorial drawing, and preparation of drawings. Part II of II. (Credit will not be awarded for both CAD 152 and DRF 152 .)

courses.title: Blueprint Reading I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 0 -1 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches the application of basic principles, visualization, orthographic projection, detail of drafting shop processes and terminology, assembly drawings and exploded views. Considers dimensioning, changes and corrections, classes of fits, tolerances and allowances, sections and convention in blueprint reading. (Credit will not be awarded for both CAD 161 and DRF 161 .)

courses.title: Computer Aided Drafting and Design I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 4-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches computer-aided drafting concepts and equipment designed to develop a general understanding of components of a typical CAD system and its operation. (Credit will not be awarded for both CAD 201 and DRF 201 .)

courses.title: Computer Aided Drafting and Design II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 4-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches production drawings and advanced operations in computer aided drafting. (Credit will not be awarded for both CAD 202 and DRF 202 .)

courses.title: Computer Aided Drafting and Design III
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 4-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches advanced CAD applications. Includes customization and/or use of advanced software. (Credit will not be awarded for both CAD 203 and DRF 203 .)

courses.title: Advanced Technical Drafting I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 4-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches use of drafting equipment and applications, emphasizing knowledge and skill required for industrial drawing. Includes piping, gearing, geometric and positional tolerances and 2D/3D drawing layout. (Credit will not be awarded for both CAD 211 and DRF 211 .)

courses.title: Advanced Technical Drafting II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 4-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches concepts of sheet metal fabrication including radii, fillets and tolerances, electrical and electronics symbols and drawing, and advanced design drafting techniques. (Credit will not be awarded for both CAD 212 and DRF 212 .)

courses.title: Computer Aided Drafting I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 3-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches computer aided drafting concepts and equipment designed to develop a general understanding of components and operate a typical CAD system. (Credit will not be awarded for both CAD 231 and DRF 231 .)

courses.title: Computer Aided Modeling and Rendering I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on training students in the contemporary techniques of 3D modeling, rendering, and animation on the personal computer. Introduces the principles of visualization, sometimes known as photo-realism, which enables the student to create presentation drawings for both architectural and industrial product design. Uses computer animation to produce walk-throughs that will bring the third dimension to architectural designs. Part I of II. (Credit will not be awarded for both CAD 238 and DRF 238 .)

courses.title: Parametric Solid Modeling I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 4-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on teaching students the design of parts by parametric solid modeling. Topics covered will include, but not limited to, sketch profiles; geometric and dimensional constraints; 3-D features; model generation by extrusion, revolution and sweep; and the creation of 2-D drawing views that include sections, details and auxiliary. Part I of II. (Credit will not be awarded for both CAD 241 and DRF 241 .)

courses.title: Parametric Solid Modeling II
courses.description: Focuses on teaching students the design of parts by parametric solid modeling. Topics covered will include, but not limited to, sketch profiles; geometric and dimensional constraints; 3-D features; model generation by extrusion, revolution and sweep; and the creation of 2-D drawing views that include sections, details and auxiliary. Part II of II. (Credit will not be awarded for both CAD 242 and DRF 242 .)

courses.title: Parametric Solid Modeling III
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week. Prerequisites: CAD 241 or DRF 241 , and CAD 242 or DRF 242 .
courses.description: Focuses on teaching students the software for the design of parts and assemblies by means of advanced parametric solid modeling to include advanced mechanical drafting techniques and building mechanical assemblies.(Credit will not be awarded for both CAD 243 and DRF 243 .)

courses.title: Design Capstone Project
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours per week. Prerequisites: CAD 211 or 212, and CAD 199 or 201.
courses.description: Focuses on design projects developed in independently and in consultation with the Instructor. Topics covered but not limited t, parametric modeling, civil, mechanical piping, architectural applications, structural, electro-mechanical, 3-D Solids, exploration of application software and the integration of CAD/CAM. (Credit will not be awarded for both CAD 280 and DRF 280 .)

courses.title: Language Arts for Young Children
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Emphasizes the early development of children's language and literacy skills. Presents techniques and methods for supporting all aspects of communication and emergent reading and writing. Addresses equitable and inclusive strategies for intervention and support.

courses.title: Introduction to Early Childhood Education
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces early childhood development through activities and experiences in early childhood, pre-kindergarten, kindergarten, and primary programs. Investigates classroom organization and procedures, and use of classroom time and materials, approaches to education for young children, professionalism, and curricular procedures.

courses.title: Creative Activities for Children
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Prepares individuals to work with young children in the arts and other creative age-appropriate activities. Investigates affective classroom experiences and open-ended activities.

courses.title: Teaching Art, Music, and Movement to Children
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on children's exploration, play, and creative expression in the areas of art, music, and movement. Emphasis will be on developing strategies for using various open-ended media representing a range of approaches in creative thinking. Addresses strategies for intervention and support for exceptional children and English Language Learners.

courses.title: Math, Science, and Social Studies for Children
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides experiences in content, methods, and materials for the development of math, science, and social studies skills in children. Emphasis will be on developing strategies for using various resources to facilitate children's construction of knowledge. Addresses strategies for intervention and support for all children.

courses.title: Working with Infants and Toddlers in Inclusive Settings
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines developmental and behavioral principles and practices and how these provide the most developmentally suitable curriculum and learning environment for very young children. Includes working with very young children with typical development, as well as those who are gifted, or have developmental delays or disabilities.

courses.title: Observation and Participation in Early Childhood/Primary Settings
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on observation as the primary method for gathering information about children in early childhood settings. Emphasizes development of skills in the implementation of a range of observation techniques. Includes minimum 30 hours of field placement in early learning setting.

courses.title: Infant and Toddler Programs
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines the care and education of infants and toddlers from birth to 36 months in group settings. Focuses on development in the physical, cognitive, social, emotional, and language domains and other factors related to working with infants/toddlers and their families. Emphasizes the importance of the environment and relationships for healthy brain development during the child's first three years of life. Investigates regulatory standards for infant/toddler care giving.

courses.title: Guiding the Behavior of Children
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Emphasizes social development and guidance. Presents practices that are respectful and meet the emotional needs of individual children. Addresses strategies for communicating expectations, promoting prosocial behaviors, preventing, and minimizing behavioral challenges through careful planning of the learning environment, curriculum, and teacher guidance.

courses.title: Children with Exceptionalities
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Reviews the history of and legal requirements for providing intervention and educational services for young children with special needs. Studies the characteristics of children with a diverse array of needs and developmental abilities. Explores concepts of early intervention, inclusion, guiding behavior and adapting environments to meet children's needs.

courses.title: Early Learning, Family, Community and Social Change
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Explores methods of developing positive, effective partnerships with families to enhance their developmental goals for children. Describes risk and protective factors and identifies community resources. Considers culture and other diverse needs, perspectives, and abilities of families and educators. Emphasizes advocacy and public policy awareness as an important role of early childhood educators.

courses.title: Advanced Observation and Participation in Early Childhood/Primary Settings
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on implementation of activity planning and observation of children through participation in early childhood settings. Emphasizes responsive teaching practices and assessment of children's development. Reviews legal and ethical implications of working with children. Supports the student in creating a professional educational portfolio. Includes minimum 30 hours of field placement in early learning setting.

courses.title: Administration of Childcare Programs
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines the skills needed for establishing and managing early childhood programs. Emphasizes professionalism and interpersonal skills, program planning, staff selection and development, creating policies, budgeting, and developing forms for recordkeeping.
