courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Requires completion of a project or research report related to the student's occupational objectives and a study of approaches to the selection and pursuit of career opportunities in the field.

courses.title: Supervised Study
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Assigns problems for independent study incorporating previous instruction and supervised by the instructor.

courses.title: Personal Finance
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents a framework of personal money management concepts, including establishing values and goals, determining sources of income, managing income, preparing a budget, developing consumer buying ability, using credit, understanding savings and insurance, providing for adequate retirement, and estate planning.

courses.title: Principles of Securities Investment
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides an introduction to the fundamentals of the security investment process. Reviews the investment strategy associated with various types of stock orders, discusses the Fundamental and Technical approaches to common stock analysis and examines bond and preferred stock pricing mechanisms. Also reviews the unique aspects of derivative security, mutual fund, real estate, and limited partnership investments.

courses.title: Personal Investments
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines personal financial investments, money management and risk reward strategies. Covers most widely employed investment instruments, including current information on stocks, bonds, mutuals, real estate, limited partnerships and tax sheltering devices.

courses.title: Topics In
courses.contact_hours: May be used also for special honors courses. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Provides an opportunity to explore topical areas of interest to or needed by students.

courses.title: Supervised Study
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Assigns problems for independent study incorporating previous instruction and supervised by the instructor.

courses.title: Financial Management
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces basic financial management topics including statement analysis, working capital; capital budgeting, and long-term financing. Focuses on Net Present Value and Internal Rate of Return techniques, lease vs. buy analysis, and Cost of Capital computations. Uses problems and cases to enhance skills in financial planning and decision making.

courses.title: Topics In
courses.contact_hours: May be used also for special honors courses. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Provides an opportunity to explore topical areas of interest to or needed by students.

courses.title: Beginning French I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces cultural awareness, listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills and emphasizes basic sentence structure. Part I of II. This is a UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Beginning French II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4 hours. Total 4 hours per week. Prerequisite: FRE 101 , or two years of successful completion of high school French, or demonstrated experiential learning, or by placement test, or equivalent.
courses.description: Introduces cultural awareness, listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills and emphasizes basic sentence structure. Part II of II. This is a UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Conversation in French I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: FRE 102 .
courses.description: Emphasizes the spoken language, stressing fluency and correctness of structure, pronunciation, and vocabulary. Part I of II.

courses.title: Conversation in French II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: FRE 102 .
courses.description: Emphasizes the spoken language, stressing fluency and correctness of structure, pronunciation, and vocabulary. Part II of II.

courses.title: Intermediate French I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: FRE 102 , or three years of successful completion of high school French, or demonstrated experiential learning, or by placement test, or equivalent.
courses.description: Continues to develop cultural awareness, listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills, and introduces complex sentence structures. Classes may be conducted in target language. Part I of II. This is a UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Intermediate French II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: FRE 201 , or four years of successful completion of high school French, or demonstrated experiential learning, or by placement test, or equivalent.
courses.description: Continues to develop cultural awareness, listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills, and emphasizes complex sentence structures. Classes may be conducted in the target language. Part II of II. This is a UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Intermediate French I-II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week. Prerequisite: FRE 102 or equivalent.
courses.description: Continues to develop understanding, speaking, reading, and writing skills. Part II of II.

courses.title: Intermediate Conversation I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: FRE 202 or assessment by instructor.
courses.description: Continues to develop fluency through emphasis on idioms and other complex sentence structures. Part I of II

courses.title: Intermediate Conversation II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: FRE 211 or assessment of instructor.
courses.description: Continues to develop fluency through emphasis on idioms and other complex sentence structures. Part II of II.

courses.title: Principles of Emergency Services
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides an overview to fire protection; career opportunities in fire protection and related fields; philosophy and history of fire protection/service; fire loss analysis; organization and function to public and private fire protection services; fire departments as part of local government; laws and regulations affecting the fire service; fire service nomenclature; specific fire protection functions; basic fire chemistry and physics; introduction to fire protection systems; introduction to fire strategy and tactics.

courses.title: Fire Behavior and Combustion
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Explores the theories and fundamentals of how and why fires start, spread, and how they are controlled.

courses.title: Hazardous Materials Chemistry
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides basic fire chemistry relating to the categories of hazardous materials including problems of recognition, reactivity, and health encountered by firefighters.

courses.title: Fire Prevention
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides fundamental information regarding the history and philosophy of fire prevention, organization and operation of a fire prevention bureau, use of fire codes, identification and correction of fire hazards, and the relationships of fire prevention with built-in fire protection systems, fire investigation, and fire and life-safety education.

courses.title: Occupational Safety and Health for the Fire Service
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the basic concepts of occupational health and safety as it relates to emergency service organizations. Includes risk evaluation and control procedures for fire stations, training sites, emergency vehicles, and emergency situations involving fire, EMS, hazardous materials, and technical rescue. (Upon completion of this course, students should be able to establish and manage a safety program in an emergency service organization.

courses.title: Fire Protection Hydraulics and Water Supply
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides a foundation of theoretical knowledge in order to understand the principles of the use of water in fire protection and to apply hydraulic principles to analyze and to solve water supply problems.

courses.title: Building Construction for Fire Protection
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides the components of building construction that relate to fire and life safety. Focuses on firefighter safety. Covers the elements of construction and design of structures and how they are key factors when inspecting buildings, preplanning fire operations, and operating at emergencies.

courses.title: Strategy and Tactics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides an in-depth analysis of the principles of fire control through utilization of personnel, equipment, and extinguishing agents on the fire ground.

courses.title: Introduction to Physical Geography
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines the global patterns and processes of the atmosphere, biosphere, lithosphere, and hydrosphere. Explores Earth?s physical systems and the interrelationships among them through studying Earth-Sun geometry, climate and weather phenomena, landforms, biomes, and environmental change.

courses.title: People and the Land: Intro to Cultural Geography
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides an introduction to themes in human geography and the ways in which human geographers study spatial relationships in the world. Emphasizes geospatial tools and concepts to examine global patterns of human demographics, culture, geopolitics, and economic and environmental interdependence through introduction to a broad range of subject matter. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: World Regional Geography
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines similarities and differences among the world's major regions. Evaluates ways in which people and places interact across space and time to produce particular spatial and environmental patterns. Introduces the student to geographic tools such as maps. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Political Geography
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines the influence of geography on political systems and nation states. Discusses historic and current events including campaigns, wars, trade, and treaties as functions of land, resources and energy requirements. Introduces students to types and uses of maps

courses.title: Coordinated Internship
courses.contact_hours: Credit/practice ratio not to exceed 1:5 hours. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Supervises on-the-job training in selected business, industrial or service firms coordinated by the college.

courses.title: Topics In
courses.contact_hours: May be used also for special honors courses. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Provides an opportunity to explore topical areas of interest to or needed by students.

courses.title: On-Site Training
courses.contact_hours: Credit/work ratio not to exceed 1:5 hours. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Specializes in career orientation and training program without pay in selected businesses and industry, supervised and coordinated by the college.

courses.title: Cooperative Education
courses.contact_hours: Credit/work ratio not to exceed 1:5 hours. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Supervises in on-the-job training for pay in approved business, industrial and service firms, coordinated by the college's cooperative education office. Is applicable to all occupational- technical curricula at the discretion of the college.

courses.title: Seminar and Project
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Requires completion of a project or research report related to the student's occupational objectives and a study of approaches to the selection and pursuit of career opportunities in the field.

courses.title: Supervised Study
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Assigns problems for independent study incorporating previous instruction and supervised by the instructor.

courses.title: Beginning German I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces cultural awareness, listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills and emphasizes basic sentence structure. Part I of II. This is a UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Beginning German II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4 hours. Total 4 hours per week. Prerequisite: GER 101 , or two years of successful completion of high school German, or demonstrated experiential learning, or by placement test, or equivalent.
courses.description: Introduces cultural awareness, listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills and emphasizes basic sentence structure. Part II of II. This is a UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Intermediate German I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: GER 102 , or three years of successful completion of high school German, or demonstrated experiential learning, or by placement test, or equivalent.
courses.description: Continues to develop cultural awareness, listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills, and introduces complex sentence structures. Classes may be conducted in target language. Part I of II. This is a UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Intermediate German II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: GER 201 , or four years of successful completion of high school German, or demonstrated experiential learning, or by placement test, or equivalent.
courses.description: Continues to develop cultural awareness, listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills, and emphasizes complex sentence structures. Classes may be conducted in the target language. Part II of II. This is UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Introduction to Geospatial Technology I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: Basic Computer Literacy.
courses.description: Provides an introduction to the concepts of Geographic Information Systems (GIS), Global Positioning Systems, (GPS) and remote sensing components of Geospatial Technology. Teaches the introductory concepts of geographic location and problem solving by using GIS and GPS units in demonstrating solutions to cross-curricular applications of the technology. Part I of II.

courses.title: Topics In
courses.contact_hours: May be used also for special honors courses. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Provides an opportunity to explore topical areas of interest to or needed by students.

courses.title: Geographical Information Systems I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 - 3 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 - 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides hands-on introduction to a dynamic desktop GIS (Geographic Information System). Introduces the components of a desktop GIS and their functionality. Emphasizes manipulation of data for the purpose of analysis, presentation, and decision-making.

courses.title: Physical Geology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the science of physical geology through a comprehensive systems-based examination of Earth's structure, composition, rocks and minerals, landforms, geomorphology, and agents responsible for shaping and modifying its environments. Explores the origin and evolution of Earth's topographic and bathymetric features, geologic phenomena, and geologic hazards, resulting from plate tectonics. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Historical Geology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Traces the evolution of the earth and life through time. Presents scientific theories of the origin of the earth and life and interprets rock and fossil record. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Oceanography I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines the dynamics of the oceans and ocean basins. Applies the principles of physical, chemical, biological, and geological oceanography. Part I of II.

courses.title: Oceanography II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines the dynamics of the oceans and ocean basins. Applies the principles of physical, chemical, biological, and geological oceanography. Part II of II.

courses.title: Field Studies in Geology
courses.contact_hours: Field studies 3-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Investigates geologic phenomena. Includes activities such as observation of regional geology and landforms, collection of samples, and measurement and interpretation of geologic structures.

courses.title: Supervised Study
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Assigns problems for independent study incorporating previous instruction and supervised by the instructor.

courses.title: Environmental Geology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week. Prerequisite: GOL 105 .
courses.description: Explores the interaction between man and his physical environment. Stresses geologic hazards and environmental pollution utilizing case histories.

courses.title: Seminar and Project
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Requires completion of a project or research report related to the student's occupational objectives and a study of approaches to the selection and pursuit of career opportunities in the field.

courses.title: Supervised Study
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Assigns problems for independent study incorporating previous instruction and supervised by the instructor.

courses.title: Health Information Technology I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces values, uses and content of the medical record. Defines numbering, filling and retention policies and practices.

courses.title: Health Information Technology II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Laboratory 1 hour. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces principles of data quality and validation types and uses of health databases.

courses.title: Medical Terminology I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the student to the language used in the health record. Includes a system-by-system review of anatomical disease, and operative terms, abbreviations, radiography procedures, laboratory tests, and pharmacology terms. Part I of II.

courses.title: Medical Terminology II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours per week.
courses.description: Continues with focus on the language used in the health record. Includes a system-by-system review of anatomic disease, and operative terms, abbreviations, radiography procedures, laboratory tests, and pharmacology terms. Part II of II.

courses.title: Medical Terminology and Disease Processes I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Includes the study of prefixes, suffixes, stem words, and technical terms; puts emphasis on the causes and treatment of selected disease processes. Part I of II.

courses.title: Introduction to Medical Practice Management
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces principles of administrative practice management. Examines patient scheduling, records management, financial systems and other systems/procedures. Focuses on the development of organizations and decision making skills utilized by the practice manager.

courses.title: Reimbursement Issues in Medical Practice Management
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces major reimbursement systems in the United States. Focuses on prospective payment systems, managed care, and documentation necessary for appropriate reimbursement. Emphasizes management of practice to avoid fraud.

courses.title: Anatomy and Physiology for Administrative Health Professionals
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: Medical Terminology or HLT 143 or HIM 111 .
courses.description: Introduces the structure and function of the systems of the human body as applied by administrative health professionals.

courses.title: Health Statistics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the student to basic statistical principles and calculations as applied in the health care environment, procedures for collection and reporting vital statistics, and basic quality control basics.

courses.title: Legal Aspects of Health Record Documentation
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents the legal requirements associated with health record documentation. Emphasizes the policies and procedures concerning the protection of the confidentiality of patient's health records.

courses.title: Performance Improvement in Health Care Settings
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on concepts of facility wide performance improvement, resource management and risk management. Applies tools for data collection and analysis.

courses.title: Electronic Health Records Management
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week. Prerequisites: HIM 130 and HIM 230 .
courses.description: Studies new trends in management and processing of health information with emphasis on the electronic health record (EHR). Covers the definition, benefits, standards, functionality, confidentiality and security, and impact of the EHR in the healthcare environment. Explores implementation of the EHR including infrastructure required, project management techniques, information technology systems, workflow processes and redesign in various health care settings. Discusses legal issues created by implementation of the EHR.

courses.title: Health Records Coding
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines the development of coding classification systems. Introduces ICD-9-CM coding classification system, its format and conventions. Stresses basic coding steps and guidelines according to body systems. Provides actual coding exercises in relation to each system covered.

courses.title: Advanced Coding and Reimbursement
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on the applications and evaluation of advanced coding skills through practical exercises using actual healthcare data; while examining the components of DRGs, APCs and APGs and other prospective payment in the healthcare environment. Utilizes current coding standards in identifying payment methodologies, revenue cycle management and reimbursement.

courses.title: Facility Based Medical Coding
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Students will learn to accurately assign CPT, ICD-9 Level 1, 2 and 3, in addition to HCPCS codes for inpatient, outpatient facility, and ambulatory surgical centers according to guidelines and rules set forth by the cooperating parties. Students will apply the theory and regulations concerning prospective payment systems (in and out of the facility setting) APC and DRG assignment.

courses.title: Coordinated Internship
courses.contact_hours: Variable hours per week.
courses.description: Supervises on-the-job training in selected business, industrial or service firms coordinated by the college. Credit/practice ratio not to exceed 1:5 hours. May be repeated for credit.

courses.title: Western Civilizations Pre-1600 CE
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines the development of western civilization from ancient times to 1600 CE. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Western Civilizations Post-1600 CE
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines the development of western civilization from 1600 CE to the present. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: World Civilizations Pre-1500 CE
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Surveys the history of Asia, Africa, the Americas, and Europe from antiquity to approximately 1500. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: World Civilizations Post-1500 CE
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Surveys the history of Asia, Africa, Europe, and the Americas from approximately 1500 CE through the present. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: United States History to 1877
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the history of the United States from its origins to 1877. Includes the European exploration, development of the American colonies and their institutions, the Revolution, major political, social and economic developments, geographical expansion, the Civil War, and Reconstruction. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: United States History Since 1865
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the history of the United States from 1865 to present. Includes major political, social and economic developments since 1865, overseas expansion, the two world wars, the Cold War and the post-Cold War era. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: History of the American Indian
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines the history and culture of the native peoples of the Americas.

courses.title: Women in World History
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies the role of women and attitudes toward women from ancient times to the present.

courses.title: Women in American History
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies the role of women and attitudes toward women in American society from colonial times to the present.

courses.title: History of the Contemporary World
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Analyzes world developments since World War II.

courses.title: African-American History I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Surveys the history of African Americans from their African origins to 1876.

courses.title: African-American History II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Surveys the history of black Americans from their African origins to the present. Part II of II.

courses.title: Seminar and Project
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Requires completion of a project or research report related to the student's occupational objectives and a study of approaches to the selection and pursuit of career opportunities in the field.

courses.title: Supervised Study
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Assigns problems for independent study incorporating previous instruction and supervised by the instructor.

courses.title: History of African Civilization
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines major social, economic, political and religious developments across the African continent from earliest times to the present. The assignments in the course require college-level reading fluency and coherent communication through written reports.

courses.title: History of African Civilizations II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines major social, economic, political and religious developments from earliest times to the present. Part II of II.

courses.title: Local History
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies the history of the local community and/or region.

courses.title: Topics in European History I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines selected topics in the history of Europe from ancient times to the present. Part I of II.

courses.title: Topics in European History II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines selected topics in the history of Europe from ancient times to the present. Part II of II.

courses.title: Introduction to Latin American History
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines the development of Latin American civilizations from the pre-Columbian era to the present

courses.title: History of Russia I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Surveys history of Russia from earliest times to the present. Includes political, economic, multi-national, social, and cultural aspects of Russian and Soviet history. Part I of II.

courses.title: History of Middle East Civilization I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Surveys intellectual, cultural, social, economic and religious patterns in the civilizations of the Middle East. Covers Semitic, Indo-European, and Turkic-speaking peoples from pre-Islamic to the present. Part I of II.

courses.title: History of Middle East Civilization II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Surveys intellectual, cultural, social, economic and religious patterns in the civilizations of the Middle East. Covers Semitic, Indo-European, and Turkic-speaking peoples from pre-Islamic to the present. Part II of II.

courses.title: History of Modern East Asian Civilizations
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines East Asian civilizations from the early modern period through the present day.

courses.title: Topics in Cultural Ethnicity I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Cultural experiences of various ethnic groups in the United States, e.g. the Irish, Italians, Jews, Germans, etc.

courses.title: United States History in Film
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines selected topics in the United States history which shaped the American experience, presented in film.

courses.title: Military History of the Civil War
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Analyzes military campaigns of the Civil War, including factors contributing to the defeat of the Confederacy and problems created by the war. May include field trips to Civil War sites in the region.

courses.title: The Second World War
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines causes and consequences of the Second World War. Includes the rise of totalitarianism, American neutrality, military developments, the home fronts, diplomacy, and the decision to use the atomic bomb.

courses.title: The American Constitution
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Analyzes the origin and development of the United States Constitution. Includes the evolution of civil liberties, property rights, contracts, due process, judicial review, federal-state relationships, and corporate-government relations.

courses.title: Civil War and Reconstruction
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies factors that led to the division between the States. Examines the war, the home fronts, and the era of Reconstruction.

courses.title: United States History Since World War II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Investigates United States history from 1945 to the present, studying both domestic developments and American involvement in international affairs.

courses.title: The American Experience in Vietnam
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Analyzes American involvement in Vietnam from World War II with emphasis on the presidencies of Johnson, Nixon and Ford.

courses.title: Age of the American Revolution
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines the factors that led to the separation of the American colonies from Great Britain. The course covers the events leading to the Revolutionary War, the problems faced by the revolutionary government in fighting the war, the war itself, and the postwar events leading to the adoption of the United States Constitution.

courses.title: History of Virginia
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Explores the cultural, economic, political, and religious history of Virginia from pre-contact to the present. Includes diverse perspectives to emphasize the significant contributions different groups of people (African Americans, Indigenous Peoples, European-Americans, Women) made to the history of Virginia, the colonies, and the United States.

courses.title: Studies In
courses.contact_hours: Variable hours per week.
courses.description: Covers new content not covered in existing courses in the discipline. Allows instructor to explore content and instructional methods to assess the course's viability as a permanent offering.

courses.title: Topics In
courses.contact_hours: May be used also for special honors courses. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Provides an opportunity to explore topical areas of interest to or needed by students.

courses.title: Cooperative Education
courses.contact_hours: Credit/work ratio not to exceed 1:5 hours. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Supervises in on-the-job training for pay in approved business, industrial and service firms, coordinated by the college's cooperative education office. Is applicable to all occupational- technical curricula at the discretion of the college.

courses.title: Supervised Study
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Assigns problems for independent study incorporating previous instruction and supervised by the instructor.

courses.title: First Aid and Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on the principles and techniques of safety, first aid, and cardiopulmonary resuscitation.

courses.title: Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour per week.
courses.description: Provides training in coordinated mouth-to-mouth artificial ventilation and chest compression, choking, life-threatening emergencies, and sudden illness. Equivalent to EMS 100 .

courses.title: First Aid and Safety
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on the principles and techniques of safety and first aid.

courses.title: Personal and Community Health
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces students to the basic concepts of health and dimensions of wellness through exploration of a variety of personal health topics. Identifies factors that affect the health status of individuals in addition to health promotion and disease prevention at the personal and community level.

courses.title: Introduction to Personal and Community Health
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour per week.
courses.description: Introduces and focuses on the principles of personal and community health.

courses.title: Introduction to Personal Wellness Concepts
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces students to the dimensions of wellness including the physical, emotional, environmental, spiritual, occupational, and social components.

courses.title: Substance Abuse: Prevention and Treatment
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Explores the use and abuse of drugs in contemporary society with emphasis upon sociological, physiological, and psychological effects of drugs.

courses.title: Anatomy and Physiology for Exercise Science
courses.contact_hours: 3 Credits, 3 Hours Lecture, 3 Contact Hours
courses.description: Presents basic principles of human anatomy and physiology including the body structure, systems and functions. The course provides a foundation to build and apply concepts in the study of Exercise Science, Group Fitness, Personal Training, and related fitness studies.

courses.title: Child Health and Nutrition
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on the physical needs of the preschool child and the methods by which these are met. Emphasizes health routines, hygiene, nutrition, feeding and clothing habits, childhood diseases, and safety as related to health growth and development.

courses.title: Orientation to Health Related Professions
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Total 1- 2 hours per week.
courses.description: Explores the interrelated roles and functions of various members of the health team.

courses.title: Medical Terminology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides an understanding of medical abbreviations and terms. Includes the study of prefixes, suffixes, word stems and technical terms with emphasis on proper spelling, pronunciation and usage.

courses.title: Medical Terminology II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides an understanding of medical abbreviations and terms. Includes the study of prefixes, suffixes, word stems, and technical terms with emphasis on proper spelling, pronunciation, and usage. Emphasizes more complex skills and techniques in understanding medical terminology. Part II of II. This course applies to career/technical education (CTE) programs. HLT 143 serves both transfer and CTE programs.

courses.title: Ethics for Health Care Personnel
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Total 1-2 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on ethical concepts of health care. Emphasizes confidentiality, maintaining patient records, personal appearance, professionalism with patients/clients, associates, and an awareness of health care facilities.

courses.title: Current Issues and Health Care
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on current issues in the health care industry.

courses.title: Health Care for Athletic Injuries
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches prevention and care of athletic injuries, recognition and management of head and spinal injuries, fractures, strains, sprains, as well as cardiac emergencies. Discusses taping, protective equipment, and medical referral.

courses.title: Personal Health and Fitness
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies the relationships between health and fitness. Topics include nutrition, disease prevention, weight control, smoking and health, medical care, aerobic and anaerobic conditioning, and the relationship between physical and mental health.

courses.title: Seminar and Project
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Requires completion of a project or research report related to the student's occupational objectives and a study of approaches to the selection and pursuit of career opportunities in the field.

courses.title: Supervised Study
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Assigns problems for independent study incorporating previous instruction and supervised by the instructor.

courses.title: Human Sexuality
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides a basic understanding of human sexuality. Includes anatomy, physiology, pregnancy, family planning, venereal diseases, and sexual variations.

courses.title: Personal Stress Management
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides a basic understanding of stress and explores its physical, psychological and social effects. Includes the relationships among stress and change, self-evaluation, sources of stress, and ways to develop current coping skills for handling stress. The assignments in the course require college-level reading fluency and coherent communication through written reports.

courses.title: Concepts of Disease
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Emphasizes general principles, classifications, causes, and treatments of selected disease processes. Intended primarily for students enrolled in health technology programs.

courses.title: Introduction to Public Health
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides an overview of public health systems in the United States and globally with an emphasis on core functions, essential services and health determinants. Explores the history, core areas and current trends within public health as well as how public health affects individuals and populations. The assignments in the course require college-level reading fluency and coherent communication through documented written reports.

courses.title: Principles of Nutrition
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces students to the basic concepts of nutrition and its impact on personal wellness. Emphasizes an evidence-based approach to various topics, such as the nutrient components of food, the components of a healthy eating pattern, and the relationship between diet and health. Provides a behavioral approach to nutrient guidelines for the development and maintenance of optimum wellness. The assignments in the course require college-level reading fluency and coherent communication through documented written reports.

courses.title: General Pharmacology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours per week.
courses.description: Emphasizes general pharmacology for the health related professions covering general principles of drug actions/reactions, major drug classes, specific agent within each class, and routine mathematical calculations needed to determine desired dosages.

courses.title: Basic Pharmacy I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Explores the basics of general pharmacy, reading prescriptions, symbols, packages, pharmacy calculations. Teaches measuring compounds of drugs, dosage forms, drug laws, and drug classifications. Part I of II.

courses.title: Basic Pharmacy II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Explores the basics of general pharmacy, reading prescriptions, symbols, packages, pharmacy calculations. Teaches measuring compounds of drugs, dosage forms, drug laws, and drug classifications. Part II of II.

courses.title: Basic Pharmacy I Lab
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides practical experience to supplement instruction in HLT 261 -262. Should be taken concurrently with HLT 261 -262, in appropriate curricula, as identified by the college. Part I of II.

courses.title: Seminar and Project
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Requires completion of a project or research report related to the student's occupational objectives and a study of approaches to the selection and pursuit of career opportunities in the field.

courses.title: Supervised Study
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Assigns problems for independent study incorporating previous instruction and supervised by the instructor.

courses.title: Introduction to Human Services
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces human service agencies, roles and careers. Presents an historical perspective of the field as it relates to human services today. Additional topics include values clarification and needs of target populations.

courses.title: Basic Counseling Skills I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Develops skills needed to function in a helping relationship. Emphasizes skills in attending, listening and responding. Clarifies personal skill strengths, deficits and goals for skill improvement.

courses.title: Basic Counseling Skills II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per work.
courses.description: Expands the development of counseling skills needed to function effectively in a helping relationship. Emphasizes skills in responding, personalizing, summarizing and initiating. Clarifies personal skill strengths, deficits and goals for skill improvement. Develops plans for achieving personal and program goals.

courses.title: Group Dynamics I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines the stages of group development, group dynamics, the role of the leader in a group, and recognition of the various types of group processes. Discusses models of group dynamics that occur as a result of group membership dynamics.

courses.title: Group Dynamics II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines group dynamics, group leadership, group cohesion, transference and group helping through experiential involvement in group facilitating and leadership. Increases group skills through active classroom participation in group experiences.

courses.title: Effects of Psychoactive Drugs
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides information on the biochemical, physiological, and behavioral aspects of substance addiction and will review the symptoms of addiction. Emphasizes areas of chemical dependency, medical epidemiology, physiological threats of addiction and methods of identifying multiple drug abusers.

courses.title: Coordinated Internship
courses.contact_hours: Credit/practice ratio not to exceed 1:5 hours. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Supervises on-the-job training in selected business, industrial or service firms coordinated by the college.

courses.title: Functional Family Intervention
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides an understanding of functions and dysfunctions within the family. Emphasizes the development of effective skills through an interpersonal/interactional approach to family intervention.

courses.title: Helping Across Cultures
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides an historical overview of selected cultural and racial groups. Promotes understanding of group differences and the impact on counseling services.

courses.title: The Helper As a Change Agent
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches the following skills for implementing alternative models of change and influence: action research, problem- solving, consultation, workshop development, and outreach and advocacy for diverse client populations.

courses.title: Productive Problem-Solving
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Develops problem-solving and program-development skills needed to function in helping relationships. Emphasizes skills-training within the classroom and application of the skills in other settings.

courses.title: Gerontology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines the process of aging; its implications in relation to health, recreation, education, transportation, meaningful work or activity, and to community resources. Emphasizes experiencing the aging process, facilitating retirement, and application of the helping relationship to work with older adults.

courses.title: Substance Use Treatment I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides knowledge, skills, and insight for working in substance use programs. Emphasizes personal growth and client growth measures in helping relationships. Stresses various methods of individual and group techniques for helping the individual with substance use disorder.

courses.title: Substance Use Treatment II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: HMS 251 .
courses.description: Expands knowledge and skill in working with individuals with substance use disorder. Focuses on assisting people with substance use disorder in individual and group settings and explores client treatment modalities. May provide opportunities for field experience in treatment centers.

courses.title: Case Management and Substance Abuse
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on the process for interviewing substance abuse clients. Includes intake, assessment, handling denial, and ending the interview. Teaches skills for writing short-term goals and treatment plans with emphasis on accountability. Examines various reporting devices.

courses.title: Human Behavior I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Develops skills in working with individuals, families, groups, organizations and communities within the socio- cultural context. Emphasizes historical development of various social systems and how these systems affect the whole person. Part I of II.

courses.title: Personality Theory
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies the theories of personality and their relationship to counseling. Emphasis is on the historical perspective, view of human nature, contributions and limitations of each theory.

courses.title: Counseling Psychology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies major counseling theories, their contributions and limitations, and the application of each to a counseling interaction. Students develop their own personal counseling theory.

courses.title: Great Books I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces selected great works of philosophy and literature, with emphasis on close analysis of the text. Part I of II.

courses.title: Great Books II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces selected great works of philosophy and literature, with emphasis on close analysis of the text. Part II of II.

courses.title: Topics In
courses.contact_hours: May be used also for special honors courses. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Provides an opportunity to explore topical areas of interest to or needed by students.

courses.title: Early Humanities
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines the values and expression of ideas of selected western and non-western cultures from prehistory up to the 1300s, integrating the arts, literature, religion, and philosophy within the context of history. The assignments in this course require college-level reading, analysis of scholarly studies, and coherent communication through properly cited and formatted written reports. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Modern Humanities
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines the values and expression of ideas of selected western and non-western cultures from the 1300s until 1900s, integrating the visual arts, literature, religion, music and philosophy within the context of history. The assignments in this course require college-level reading, analysis of scholarly studies, and coherent communication through properly cited and formatted written reports. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Interdisciplinary Principles of the Humanities I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Integrates unifying principles of the humanities and related fields of study. Emphasizes the expansion of student's intellectual perspective and development of concepts enabling the integration of knowledge from diverse fields into a unified whole. Part I of II.

courses.title: Interdisciplinary Principles of the Humanities II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Integrates unifying principles of the humanities and related fields of study. Emphasizes the expansion of student's intellectual perspective and development of concepts enabling the integration of knowledge from diverse fields into a unified whole. Part II of II.

courses.title: Creative Thinking
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines, analyzes, and develops creative and critical thinking processes with individual and group applications to solve business, scientific, social, environmental, and other practical problems. The assignments in this course require college-level reading, analysis of scholarly studies, and coherent communication through properly cited and formatted written reports.

courses.title: Comparative Mythology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies the cultural expressions of mythology. Considers selected mythologies representing diverse global culture, with emphasis on parallels and divergences in structure, purpose, and representation in literature and the arts. The assignments in this course require college-level reading, analysis of scholarly studies, and coherent communication through properly cited and formatted written reports. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: The Greek and Roman Tradition
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Explores the significance of Greek and Roman cultures on the individual and society, expressed prominently from the Classical Age in Athens to its survival during Roman times. Examines the key contributions that the Greeks and Romans have imparted upon storytelling, theater, philosophy, civics, political morphology, and the arts and the impact they have in the modern world. The assignments in this course require college-level reading, analysis of scholarly studies, and coherent communication through properly cited and formatted written reports. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Contemporary Humanities
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines selected values and expressions of ideas of western and non-western cultures throughout the twentieth century and beyond, integrating the visual arts, literature, performing arts, religion, and philosophy within the context of history. The assignments in this course require college-level reading, analysis of scholarly studies, and coherent communication through properly cited and formatted written reports

courses.title: Quality Assurance Technology I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies principles and techniques of quality engineering for the management, design engineering economics, production, and assurance of quality. Emphasizes fundamentals of total quality assurance for product and process control. May include design review, fundamentals of statistics procurement control, sampling and control chart systems, quality reporting, process capability analysis, tool and gauge control, document control, or troubleshooting quality control. Part I of II.

courses.title: Quality Assurance Technology II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies principles and techniques of quality engineering for the management, design engineering economics, production, and assurance of quality. Emphasizes fundamentals of total quality assurance for product and process control. May include design review, fundamentals of statistics procurement control, sampling and control chart systems, quality reporting, process capability analysis, tool and gauge control, document control, or troubleshooting quality control. Part II of II.

courses.title: Industrial Methods
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours per week.
courses.description: Covers theoretical knowledge necessary for familiarization with common handtools, common power tools, measuring tools and techniques, fastening components and procedures, grinding operations, metal cutting operations, and other miscellaneous tasks.

courses.title: Nondestructive Inspection (NDI) and Testing
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies nondestructive inspection and testing methods as they relate to industry. May include radiographic (RT), ultrasonic (UT), eddy current (ET), magnetic particle (MT), and liquid penetrant (PT) or other methods of testing.

courses.title: Industrial Engineering Technology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces basic skills required for a career in industrial engineering technology. Includes basic statistics for engineering technicians, the SI system, graphic analysis, and careers as an industrial engineering technician.

courses.title: Materials and Processes in Manufacturing I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies materials and processes for the manufacture of products. Investigates the nature of various materials. Examines the manufacturing processes of industry and their effects on materials. Part I of II.

courses.title: Materials and Processes in Manufacturing II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies materials and processes for the manufacture of products. Investigates the nature of various materials. Examines the manufacturing processes of industry and their effects on materials. Part II of II.

courses.title: Materials and Processes of Industry
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies materials and processes for the manufacture of products. Investigates the nature of various materials. Examines the manufacturing processes of industry and their effects on materials.

courses.title: Installation and Preventive Maintenance
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies practices in the installation of machinery, including mounting, grouting, leveling, and alignment. Examines methods of preventive maintenance including inspection, scheduled maintenance, controls, record keeping, repair parts stocking, and safety considerations.

courses.title: Quality Control
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies history, structure, and organization of the quality control unit. May include incoming material control, product and process control, and cost control.

courses.title: Introduction to Metrology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies principles of measurement and calibration control, application of statistics to measurement processes, and standards of measurements in calibration. May include the use of gauges and instruments in modern production and dimensional control concepts.

courses.title: Statistical Quality Control
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies essentials and application of statistics in quality control function. May include definitions and uses of averages, standard deviations, ranges, and sampling plans. May discuss dependent and independent variables, and distribution probabilities.

courses.title: Industrial Management
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies planning, organizing, directing, and influencing industrial activities. May include research, product design, methods and time management, quality assurance and current manufacturing methodologies.

courses.title: Introduction to Robotics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 0-2 hours. Total 2-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies evolution and history of robotics with an emphasis on automated and flexible manufacturing. Presents advantages and limitations of present robot systems.

courses.title: Plant Layout and Materials Handling
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines arrangement and layout of physical facilities. Explains material handling and modern techniques for efficient utilization of space.

courses.title: Applied Quality Control
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies principles of inspection and quality assurance with emphasis on statistical process control. May include the setting up, maintaining, and interpreting of control charts, and review of basic metrology.

courses.title: Statistical Quality Control
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 1-2 hours. Total 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Gives overview of the quality control function within industry. May include the organization, cost, and techniques of quality control. Emphasizes essentials and applications of statistics in the quality control function.

courses.title: Time and Motion Study
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies principles and applications of motion analysis, process, operations, and micromotion study; methods improvement, work simplification, standardization, rating, allowance and analysis of time data.

courses.title: Introduction to Basic Computer Integrated Manufacturing
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Laboratory 3-9 hours. Total 4-9 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents basic principles used in the design and implementation in a computer integrated manufacturing system. Emphasizes team concept and all aspects of a computer integrated manufacturing system to include the following: Robotics, Conveyor Control, Machining Center Integration Quality Control, Statistical Quality Control, and Computer Integrated Manufacturing (CIM) software.

courses.title: Automated Manufacturing Systems I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-4 hours. Laboratory 0-4 hours. Total 3-6 hours per week. Prerequisite: divisional approval.
courses.description: Presents basic principles used in the design and implementation in manufacturing work cells. Includes selection of the robot system, worksite, application cell sensors, development of cycle times, and economic analysis.

courses.title: Principles of Instrumentation
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces various types of instruments and gauges used in the manufacturing processes. Examines basic principles of pneumatic, hydraulic, electronic and mechanically operated devices. Requires a report as an out-of-class activity.

courses.title: Instrumentation Fundamentals
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours, Laboratory 2 hours, Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents the preparatory fundamentals of instrumentation including hydraulics, pneumatics, instrumentation loops, and temperature. Examines the basic principles of hydraulics, pneumatics, transducers, thermometers, gauges, and calibration.

courses.title: Principles of Instrumentation
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 4-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the basic concepts and terminology of process control systems. Presents types of control systems, applicable component elements, basic control analysis, and documentation requirements for measuring instruments and signal conditioning.

courses.title: Introduction to Fluid Power
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 4-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces analysis and design of hydraulic and pneumatic control systems. Presents interpretation and application of fluid power systems, schematic diagrams, and symbols.

courses.title: Instrumentation I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 3-4 hours. Total 5-7 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents the fundamental scientific principles of process control including temperature, pressure, level, and flow measurements. Topics include transducers, thermometers, and gauges are introduced along with calibration.

courses.title: Instrumentation II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 3-4 hours. Total 5-7 hours per week.
courses.description: Continues INS 230 . Covers common techniques for measuring the dynamic response of processes. Topics include transmitters and telemetering along with process control systems.

courses.title: System Troubleshooting
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5-6 hours per week. 2-3 Credits.
courses.description: Presents system troubleshooting theory and real troubleshooting applications. Uses a hands-on approach to provide troubleshooting experience in multiple areas such as programmable logic controllers (PLC), control automation systems and process control systems.

courses.title: Process Control Integration
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 3-4 hours. Total 5-7 hours per week. Prerequisites: INS 230 and ELE 233 .
courses.description: Presents computer automation including PLCs, SCADA, and PC-based systems to control processes. Topics such as PLC control and computer data acquisition are introduced where students will use existing systems or build systems and control these systems with PLCs and computer data acquisition systems. Assesses students through test and project evaluations and the course will be assessed by graduate feedback.

courses.title: Interpreting Foundations I-II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Develops fundamental skills of interpreting, including cognitive processes and intralingual language development in English and ASL. Reviews Process Models of interpreting, and uses one to analyze interpretations. Develops feedback skills essential to the team interpreting process. Part I of II.

courses.title: Interpreting Foundations I-II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Develops fundamental skills of interpreting, including cognitive processes and intralingual language development in English and ASL. Reviews Process Models of interpreting, and uses one to analyze interpretations. Develops feedback skills essential to the team interpreting process. Part II of II.

courses.title: Translation Skills
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week. Prerequisite: INT 105 .
courses.description: Further develops fundamental skills needed for the task of interpreting Targets comprehending source language (either ASL or English), transferring content into memory store (breaking from original form), restructuring into target language, maintaining message equivalence, conveying implicit and inferred information, and applying appropriate discourse structure. Review Process Model of interpreting, and uses it to analyze translations. Further develops feedback skills essential to the team interpreting process.

courses.title: Interpreting: An Introduction to the Profession
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces basic principles and practices of interpreting, focusing on the history of the profession, logistics of interpreting situations, regulatory and legislative issues, resources, and the Code of Ethics. Describes the state quality assurance screening and national certification exam systems, including test procedures.

courses.title: ASL-to-English Interpretation I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4-5 hours per week. Prerequisite: INT 107 .
courses.description: Begins consecutively interpreting monologues from the source language (ASL) to the target language (English). Watch entire ASL monologues process them, analyze them, then choose appropriate English to match the message. Eventually interpret the monologue into English. Puts interpreting theory into practice in a lab environment. Conducts research in the field of interpretation. Develops team interpreting techniques. Interacts with consumers of ASL-English interpretation.

courses.title: English-to-ASL Interpretation I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4-5 hours per week. Prerequisite: INT 107 .
courses.description: Begins consecutively interpreting monologues from the source language (English) to the target language (ASL). Listen to entire English monologues, process them, analyze them, then choose appropriate ASL to match the message. Puts interpreting theory into practice in a lab environment. Conducts research into the field of interpretation. Develops team interpreting techniques. Encourages interaction with consumers of ASL-English interpretation.

courses.title: Transliterating I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: INT 107 .
courses.description: Studies the skills required to transmit spoken English into a manual code for English or an interpreting product with more obvious English influences, and vice versa. Introduces a variety of manual codes and their relationship to American Sign Language and Contact Signing.

courses.title: ASL-to English Interpretation II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4-5 hours per week. Prerequisites: INT 133 and INT 134 .
courses.description: Perform simultaneous interpretations of monologues in the source language (ASL) to the target language (English). Interact with consumers of interpretation.

Interact with consumers of interpretation.

courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Explores the creation of digital graphics for web design. Includes basic design elements such as color and layout will be explored utilizing a computer graphics program(s).

courses.title: Design Concepts for Mobile Applications
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides skills for designing both Web-based and stand-alone applications for wireless devices. Details discussions of the needs for applications including mobile phones and a range of rich hand-held devices such as PDA's. Emphasizes the importance of usability, accessibility, optimization and performance to create fast-loading business enterprise applications and games.

courses.title: Database Fundamentals
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the student to Relational Database and Relational Database theory. Includes planning, defining and using a database; table design, linking, and normalization; types of databases, database description and definition.

courses.title: Structured Query Language
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Incorporates a working introduction to commands, functions and operators used in SQL for extracting data from standard databases.

courses.title: Web Page Design II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Incorporates advanced techniques in web site planning, design, usability, accessibility, advanced site management, and maintenance utilizing web editor software(s).

courses.title: Interactive Web Design
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides techniques in interactive design concepts to create cross-platform, low-bandwidth animations utilizing a vector based application. Emphasizes the importance of usability, accessibility, optimization and performance.

courses.title: Advanced Database Management
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses in-depth instruction in the handling of critical tasks of planning and implementing large databases. Includes an introduction to concepts of advanced data warehousing and database configuration.

courses.title: Careers and Cyber Ethics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours per week.
courses.description: Career paths in Information Technology will be explored to help the student determine the appropriate degree plan. Career paths will include but not be limited to software development, computer science, database, networking, system administration and operations, end user support, web design, and management. The student will learn ethical concerns in business and information technology including the ACM Code of Ethics.

courses.title: Introduction to Computer Applications and Concepts
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Covers computer concepts and internet skills, and uses a software suite which includes word processing, spreadsheet, database, and presentation software to demonstrate skills. Recommended prerequisite keyboarding skills. This course applies to career/technical education (CTE) programs. ITE 152 serves both transfer and CTE programs.

courses.title: Microcomputer Software: Spreadsheets
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides first-time users with sufficient information to make practical use of spreadsheet software using the basic of building spreadsheets.

courses.title: Desktop Database Software
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Incorporates instruction in planning, defining, and using a database; performing queries; producing reports; working with multiple files; and concepts of database programming. Includes database concepts, principles of table design and table relationships, entering data, creating and using forms, using data from different sources, filtering, creating mailing labels.

courses.title: Microcomputer Software: Database Management
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents first-time users with sufficient information to make practical use of database management software using the basics of building databases. Covers specific business applications.

courses.title: Introduction to Digital and Information Literacy and Computer Applications
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Develops understanding of digital and information literacy. Introduces basic computer concepts in hardware, software, cyber, cloud, database, and operating systems. Includes hands-on experience developing word processing, spreadsheet and presentation documents. Evaluates the reliability of sources. Covers creating a simple web page. Examines topics such as social, legal, and ethical issues. This is a UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Introduction to E-Commerce
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies the culture and demographics of the Internet, on-line business strategies and the hardware and software tools necessary for Internet commerce. Includes the identification of appropriate target segments, the development of product opportunities, pricing structures, distribution channels over the Internet, and the execution of marketing strategy in computer- mediated environments. Presents case histories of successful Web applications.

courses.title: User Support/Help Desk Principles
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces a variety of tools and techniques that are used to provide user support in help desk operations. Includes help desk concepts, customer service skills, troubleshooting problems, writing for end users, help desk operations, and software, needs analysis, facilities management, and other related topics related to end user support.

courses.title: Introduction to Telecommunications
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Surveys data transmission systems, communication lines, data sets, network, modes of transmission, protocols, and interfacing. Emphasizes network structure and operation.

courses.title: Introduction to Network Concepts
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides instruction in networking media, physical and logical topologies, common networking standards and popular networking protocols. Emphasizes the TCP/IP protocol suite and related IP addressing schemes, including CIDR. Includes selected topics in network implementation, support and LAN/WAN connectivity.

courses.title: Microcomputer Operating Systems
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches use of operating system utilities and multiple-level directory structures, creation of batch files, and configuration of microcomputer environments. May include a study of graphical user interfaces.

courses.title: Personal Computer Hardware and Troubleshooting
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Includes specially designed instruction to give a student a basic knowledge of hardware and software configurations. Includes the installation of various peripheral devices as well as basic system hardware components.

courses.title: Enterprise Networking, Security, and Automation - Cisco
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 5-6 hours per week. Prerequisite: ITN 155
courses.description: Teaches students to configure, troubleshoot, and secure enterprise networks. Introduces students to virtualization, application programming interfaces (APIs) and the configuration management tools that make network automation possible.

courses.title: WAN Technologies - Cisco
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Concentrates on an introduction to Wide Area Networking (WANs). Includes WAN design, LAPB, Frame Relay, ISDN, HDLC, and PPP.

courses.title: Linux System Administration
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses instruction on the installation, configuration and administration of the Linux operating system and emphasizes the use of Linux as a network client and workstation.

courses.title: Studies In
courses.contact_hours: Variable hours per week.
courses.description: Covers new content not covered in existing courses in the discipline. Allows instructor to explore content and instructional methods to assess the course's viability as a permanent offering.

courses.title: Supervised Study
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
