courses.title: Administration of Network Resources
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on the management of local area network servers. Teaches proper structuring of security systems. Explains print queues, disk management, and other local area network (LAN) issues. Presents concerns and issues for the purchase and installation of hardware and software upgrades. Can be taught using any network operating system or a range of operating systems as a delivery tool.

courses.title: Information Storage and Management
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on advanced storage systems, protocol, and architectures including Storage Area Networks (SAN), Network Attached Storage (NAS), Fibre Channel Networks, Internet Protocol SANs (IPSAN), iSCSI, and Content Addressable Storage (CAS).

courses.title: Virtual Infrastructure: Installation and Configuration
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Explores concepts and capabilities of virtual architecture with a focus on the installation, configuration, and management of a virtual infrastructure, and Virtual Center. Covers fundamentals of virtual network design and implementation, fundamentals of storage area networks, virtual switching, virtual system management, and engineering for high availability.

courses.title: Cloud Computing: Infrastructure and Services
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours. Total 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on cloud infrastructure, deployment, security models, and the key considerations in migrating to cloud computing. Covers the technologies and processes required to build traditional, virtualized, and cloud data center environments, including computation, storage, networking, desktop and application virtualization, business continuity, security, and management.

courses.title: Network Security Basics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides instruction in the basics of network security in depth. Includes security objectives, security architecture, security models and security layers; risk management, network security policy, and security training. Includes the five security keys, confidentiality integrity, availability, accountability and auditability.

courses.title: Network Attacks, Computer Crime and Hacking
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Encompasses in-depth exploration of various methods for attacking and defending a network. Explores network security concepts from the viewpoint hackers and their attack methodologies. Includes topics about hackers, attacks, Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) malicious code, computer crime and industrial espionage.

courses.title: Network Communication, Security and Authentication
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Covers an in-depth exploration of various communication protocols with a concentration on TCP/IP. Explores communication protocols from the point of view of the hacker in order to highlight protocol weaknesses. Includes Internet architecture, routing, addressing, topology, fragmentation and protocol analysis, and the use of various utilities to explore TCP/IP.

courses.title: Network Security Layers
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides an in-depth exploration of various security layers needed to protect the network. Explores Network Security from the viewpoint of the environment in which the network operates and the necessity to secure that environment to lower the security risk to the network. Includes physical security, personnel security, operating system security, software security and database security.

courses.title: Advanced Linux Network Administration
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses instruction on the configuration and administration of the Linux operating system as a network server. Emphasizes the configuration of common network services such as routing, http, DNS, DHCP, ftp, telnet, SMB, NFS, and NIS.

courses.title: Visual Basic.NET I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Concentrates instruction in fundamentals of object-oriented programming using Visual Basic.NET and the .NET framework. Emphasizes program construction algorithm development, coding debugging, and documentation of graphical user interface applications.

courses.title: Java Programming I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Entails instruction in fundamentals of object-oriented programming using Java. Emphasizes program construction, algorithm development, coding, debugging, and documentation of console and graphical user interface applications.

courses.title: C++ Programming I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Centers instruction in fundamentals of object-oriented programming and design using C++. Emphasizes program construction, algorithm development, coding, debugging, and documentation of C++ applications.

courses.title: Client Side Scripting
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides instruction in fundamentals of Internet application design, development, and deployment using client side scripting language(s).

courses.title: Python Programming
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours. Total 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Entails instruction in fundamentals of object-oriented programming using Python. Emphasizes program construction, algorithm development, coding, debugging, and documentation of Python applications.

courses.title: Introduction to Game Design & Development
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces object-oriented game design and development. Provides overview of the electronic game design and development process and underlines the historical contest, content creation strategies, game careers, and future trends in the industry. Utilizes a game language environment to introduce game design, object-oriented paradigms, software design, software development and product testing. Teaches skills of writing a game design document and creating a game with several levels and objects. Integrate 2D animations, 3D models, sound effects, and background music as well as graphic backgrounds.

courses.title: Gaming and Simulation
courses.description: Introduces students to the concepts and applications of gaming and simulation through the use of gaming and simulation tools, as well as through basic programming skills.

courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Imparts instruction in application of advanced object-oriented techniques to application development using Java. Emphasizes database connectivity, inner classes, collection classes, networking, and threads.

courses.title: Web Scripting Languages
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week. Prerequisites: ITD 110 , ITP 100 .
courses.description: Introduces students to the principles, systems, and tools used to implement Web applications. Provides students with a comprehensive introduction to the programming tools and skills required to build and maintain interactive Web sites. Students will develop Web applications utilizing client-side and server-side scripting languages along with auxiliary tools needed for complete applications.

courses.title: Server Side Programming
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Centers around instruction in fundamentals of Internet application design, development, and deployment. Includes implementation of server component models, security, and database connectivity using server-side programming.

courses.title: Systems Analysis and Design
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on application of information technologies (IT) to system life cycle methodology, systems analysis, systems design, and system implementation practices. Covers methodologies related to identification of information requirements, feasibility in the areas of economic, technical and social requirements, and related issues are included in course content. Software applications may be used to enhance student skills.

courses.title: Programming for Cybersecurity
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours. Total 3-4 hours per week. Prerequisite: ITP 100 , Software Design
courses.description: Teaches scripting techniques for automating security tasks such as network monitoring and penetration testing using a high-level programming language common to cybersecurity professionals. Includes how to write custom tools and the basics of developing software exploits.

courses.description: Continues to develop cultural awareness, listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills, and emphasizes complex sentence structures. Classes may be conducted in the target language. Part II of II. This is a UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Library Skills for Research
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour per week.
courses.description: Introduces students to accessing, retrieving, evaluating, and applying a variety of digital and print information resources. Develops an understanding of the type of information provided in each of the information formats presented: reference, cataloged materials, magazines/journals, newspapers, and Internet sites. Provides background information, available resources, search techniques, sample searches, evaluation guides, and exams in each of the course units.

courses.title: Introduction to the Law and the Paralegal
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces various areas of law in which a paralegal may be employed. Includes study of the court system (Virginia and federal); a brief overview of criminal law, torts, family law, evidence, the U.C.C., contracts, and ethics; the role of the paralegal; and other areas of interest.

courses.title: Real Estate Law for Legal Assistants
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies law of real property and gives in-depth survey of the more common types of real estate transactions and conveyances such as deeds, contracts, leases, and deeds of trust. Focuses on drafting these various instruments and studies the system of recording and search of public documents.

courses.title: Family Law
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies elements of a valid marriage, grounds for divorce and annulment, separation, defenses, custody, support, adoptions, and applicable tax consequences. Includes property settlement agreements, pre- and ante-nuptial agreements, pleadings, and rules of procedure. May include specific federal and Virginia consumer laws.

courses.title: Legal Research
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides an understanding of various components of a law library, and emphasizes research skills through the use of digests, encyclopedias, reporter systems, codes, citations, ALR, and other research tools. May include research through electronic databases, overview of computer applications, and writing projects.

courses.title: Legal Writing
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: ENG 111 or permission of instructor.
courses.description: Studies proper preparation of various legal documents, including legal memoranda, letters, and pleadings. Involves practical applications. May include case and appellate briefs.

courses.title: Legal Research and Writing
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: ENG 111 or permission of division.
courses.description: Provides a basic understanding of legal research and the proper preparation of legal documents, including brief writing.

courses.title: Law Office Administration and Management
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces management principles and systems applicable to law firms, including record keeping, disbursements, escrow accounts, billing, and purchasing. May include accounting methods and software packages applicable to law firms.

courses.title: Ethics for the Paralegal
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-3 hours. Total 1-3 hour per week.
courses.description: Examines general principles of ethical conduct applicable to paralegals. Includes the application of rules of ethics to the practicing paralegal.

courses.title: Virginia and Federal Procedure
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines the rules of procedure in the Virginia and federal court systems, including the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure and the Rules of Practice and Procedure in the District Court, Circuit Court, Court of Appeals, and Supreme Court of Virginia.

courses.title: Torts
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies fundamental principles of the law of torts and may include preparation and use of pleadings and other documents involved in the trial of a civil action. Emphasizes intentional torts, negligence, personal injury, products liability, and malpractice cases.

courses.title: Trial Preparation and Discovery Practice
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines the trial process, including the preparation of a trial notebook, pretrial motions, and orders. May include preparation of interrogatories, depositions, and other discovery tools used in assembling evidence in preparation for the trial or an administrative hearing.

courses.title: Trial Practice and the Law of Evidence
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hour per week.
courses.description: Introduces civil and criminal evidence, including kinds, degrees and admissibility of evidence. Studies methods and techniques of evidence acquisition. Emphasizes Virginia and federal rules of evidence. Focuses on the elements and various problems associated with the trial of a civil or criminal case.

courses.title: Criminal Law
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on major crimes, including their classification, elements of proof, intent, conspiracy, responsibility, parties, and defenses. Emphasizes Virginia law. May include general principles of applicable constitutional law and criminal procedure.

courses.title: Administrative Practice and Procedure
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Surveys applicable administrative laws, including the Privacy Act, the Administrative Process Act, and Freedom of Information Act. Studies practice and procedure involving the Department of Alcoholic Beverage Control, State Corporation Commission, Virginia Workers' Compensation Commission, Social Security Administration, Virginia Employment Commission, and other administrative agencies.

courses.title: Estate Planning and Probate
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces various devices used to plan an estate, including wills, trust, joint ownership and insurance. Considers various plans in light of family situations and estate objectives. Focuses on practices involving administration of an estate including taxes and preparation of forms.

courses.title: Real Estate Abstracting
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Reviews aspects of abstracting title to real estate, recordation of land transactions, liens, grantor-grantee indices, warranties, covenants, restrictions, and easements.

courses.title: Real Estate Settlement Practicum
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on methods and practices in administrative area of real estate closings, back title information, preliminary report from attorney's title notes, lender's requirements, payoffs, HUD-1 settlement statement, real estate taxes, interest, escrow, disbursement and release of liens of record.

courses.title: Legal Transactions
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents an in-depth study of general contract law, including formation, breach, enforcement, and remedies. May include an overview of UCC sales, commercial paper, and collections.

courses.title: Legal Aspects of Business Organizations
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies fundamental principles of agency law and the formation of business organizations. Includes sole proprietorships, partnerships, corporation, limited liability companies, and other business entities. Reviews preparation of the documents necessary for the organization and operation of businesses.

courses.title: Elder Law
courses.contact_hours: Credits: 3 Lecture Hours: 3 Lab Hours: 0 Contact Hours: 3
courses.description: Explores the legal issues affecting the elderly population, including Social Security, Supplemental Security Income (SSI), Medicare, Medicaid, long-term care insurance, retirement housing and long-term care options, age discrimination, elder abuse and neglect, and estate and planning issues related to incapacity-guardianship, advanced medical directives, power of attorney, and end-of-life decisions.

courses.title: Machine Shop I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4-5 hours. Laboratory 9 hours. Total 13-14 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the machinist to identification, care, and use of precision tools and instruments. Emphasizes the operation of the drill press, lathe, power saw, grinder, and milling machine. Covers the sharpening of lathe curing tools, safety, and good housekeeping. Provides for operation and setup on the various types of precision grinders, milling machines, and drill presses. Part I of II.

courses.title: Machine Shop II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4-5 hours. Laboratory 9 hours. Total 13-14 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the machinist to identification, care, and use of precision tools and instruments. Emphasizes the operation of the drill press, lathe, power saw, grinder, and milling machine. Covers the sharpening of lathe curing tools, safety, and good housekeeping. Provides for operation and setup on the various types of precision grinders, milling machines, and drill presses. Part II of II.

courses.title: Machine Shop Operations
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours. Laboratory 15 hours. Total 18-19 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces bench work, sawing, drilling, lathe, milling, grinding, precision instruments, and safety. Requires solutions of related problems and preparation of weekly laboratory reports.

courses.title: Technology of Machining
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours. Laboratory 15 hours. Total 18-19 hours per week.
courses.description: Offers practice in bench work, sawing, drilling, lathe, milling, grinding, and precision measuring instruments. May require solutions of related problems and preparation of weekly laboratory reports.

courses.title: Computer Numerically Controlled (CNC) Grinding
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour, Laboratory 3 hours, Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides students with the opportunity to demonstrate proper techniques in computer numerically controlled (CNC) outside diameter (OD), internal diameter (ID), and surface grinding. Covers the programming and operation of various CNC grinders and the set-up of selected grinding operations. Focuses on understanding the importance of machine parameters and wheel selection to surface finish in grinding applications.

courses.title: Machine Trade Theory and Computation I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Covers shop theory and mathematics dealing with fractional and precision measuring tools. Includes layout, bandsaws, drill presses, the twist drill, thread cutting, taper turning, vertical and horizontal milling machines, lathe tool bit geometry, the engine lathe, and other lathe operations. Part I of II.

courses.title: Machinist Handbook
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours per week.
courses.description: Uses the machinist handbook as a ready reference book of tabular data, formulas, designs and processes relating to machine technology.

courses.title: Numerical Control I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 3-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on numerical control techniques in metal forming and machine processes. Includes theory and practice in lathe and milling machine computer numerical control program writing, setup and operation. Part I of II.

courses.title: Numerical Control II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 3-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on numerical control techniques in metal forming and machine processes. Includes theory and practice in lathe and milling machine computer numerical control program writing, setup and operation. Part II of II.

courses.title: Computer Numerical Control III
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 3-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on numerical control techniques in metal forming and machine processes. Includes theory and practice in lathe and milling machine computer numerical control program writing, setup and operation.

courses.title: Introduction to Geometrical Dimensioning and Tolerancing in Machining
courses.contact_hours: Lecture hours 3 per week.
courses.description: Focuses on basic topics in geometrical dimensioning and tolerancing (GD&T). Covers internationally recognized GD&T symbols. Explains the importance of a feature control frame. Teaches the Cartesian coordinate system in relation to precision components. Examines theoretical and practical concepts of geometric controls relative to design, tooling, production, and inspection.

courses.title: Introductory CNC Programming
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces programming of computerized numerical control machines with hands-on programming and operation of CNC machines.

courses.title: Advanced CNC Programming
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides in-depth study of programming computerized numerical control machines.

courses.title: CNC Programming
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches programming of computerized numerical control machines. Focuses on CNC machining processes.

courses.title: Metals/Heat Treatment
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides approach to metals and their structure. Gives working knowledge of methods of treating ferrous and non- ferrous metals.

courses.title: Machine Tool Maintenance
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces tool design from a maintenance and repair standpoint. Emphasizes proper care, repair, and preventative maintenance of machine tools.

courses.title: Machine Shop Practices I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 4-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces safety procedures, bench work, hand tools, precision measuring instruments, drill presses, cut-off saws, engine lathes, manual surface grinders, and milling machines. Part I of II.

courses.title: Machine Shop Practices II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 4-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces safety procedures, bench work, hand tools, precision measuring instruments, drill presses, cut-off saws, engine lathes, manual surface grinders, and milling machines. Part II of II.

courses.title: Machine Shop Practices III
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Offers practice in the operation of the drill press, engine lathe, vertical milling machine, horizontal milling machine, and the surface grinder. Introduces practical heat treatment of directly hardenable steels commonly used in machine shops. Part I of II.

courses.title: Machine Shop Practices IV
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Offers practice in the operation of the drill press, engine lathe, vertical milling machine, horizontal milling machine, and the surface grinder. Introduces practical heat treatment of directly hardenable steels commonly used in machine shops. Part II of II.

courses.title: Machine Blueprint Reading I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces reading and interpreting blueprints and working drawings. Applies visualization of objects, sketching, and machine terminology. Part I of II.

courses.title: Machine Blueprint Reading II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces reading and interpreting blueprints and working drawings. Applies visualization of objects, sketching, and machine terminology. Part II of II.

courses.title: Production Machining Techniques
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4 hours. Laboratory 6 hours. Total 10 hours per week.
courses.description: Offers practice in advanced machine shop. Emphasizes mass production techniques and interchangeable parts manufacture. Covers setup and operation of tooling and fixtures to manufacture work pieces to specified tolerances.

courses.title: Machining Techniques
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4 hours. Laboratory 15 hours. Total 19 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches milling lathe operations, precision grinding, production tooling, and machine tool attachments.

courses.title: Precision Machining Techniques
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4 hours. Laboratory 15 hours. Total 19 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches precision layout, machining techniques, high precision grinding, measuring tool calibration, and inspection procedures.

courses.title: Advanced Machine Tool Operations I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4 hours. Laboratory 9 hours. Total 13 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on advanced lathe and mill work with concentration on fits, finishes, inspection, quality control, and basic heat treating. Includes design and construction of specific projects to determine the student's operational knowledge of all equipment. Part I of II.

courses.title: Advanced Machine Tool Operations II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4 hours. Laboratory 9 hours. Total 13 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on advanced lathe and mill work with concentration on fits, finishes, inspection, quality control, and basic heat treating. Includes design and construction of specific projects to determine the student's operational knowledge of all equipment. Part II of II.

courses.title: Advanced Machine Tool Operations III
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4 hours. Laboratory 9 hours. Total 13 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches precision grinding, grinding allowances, and electro- discharge machining.

courses.title: Advanced Precision Machining I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches machining principles and calculations necessary for the precision required by the machinist. Emphasizes advanced lathe and mill work with concentration of fits. finishes, inspection, and quality control. Includes design and construction of specific projects to determine the student's operational knowledge of all equipment. Part I of II.

courses.title: Advanced Precision Machining II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches machining principles and calculations necessary for the precision required by the machinist. Emphasizes advanced lathe and mill work with concentration of fits. finishes, inspection, and quality control. Includes design and construction of specific projects to determine the student's operational knowledge of all equipment. Part II of II.

courses.title: Advanced Machinery Procedures I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on machining principles and calculations necessary for the precision required by the machinist. Emphasizes advanced lathe and mill work with concentration on fits, finishes, inspections, and quality control. Teaches design and construction of specific projects to determine the student's operational knowledge of all equipment. Part I of II.

courses.title: Advanced Machinery Procedures II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on machining principles and calculations necessary for the precision required by the machinist. Emphasizes advanced lathe and mill work with concentration on fits, finishes, inspections, and quality control. Teaches design and construction of specific projects to determine the student's operational knowledge of all equipment. Part II of II.

courses.title: Advanced Computer Aided Manufacturing
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Laboratory 2-4 hours. Total 3-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on advanced computer aided manufacturing with emphasis on CAD-CAM interfacing, advanced 3-D, and advanced turning. Introduces quality control inspection suing coordinate measuring systems, statistical process controls and digitizers. Teaches basic and advanced fabrication programming and flexible manufacturing systems.

courses.title: Introduction to Supply Chain Strategies for Industry
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour, Laboratory 6 hours, Total 7 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on effective supply chain strategies for industry. Covers first article part inspections and production validation. Demonstrates flow cell ideology in a live flow cell production environment. Examines value stream mapping, customer/supplier roles, and quality systems in addition to proper health and safety guidelines.

courses.title: Introduction to Algebra
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Covers topics in arithmetic through introduction to variables and equations.

courses.title: Learning Support for Quantitative Reasoning
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Corequisite: MTH 154
courses.description: Provides support to ensure success for students co-enrolled in Quantitative Reasoning (MTH 154). Course will review foundational topics through direct instruction, guided practice, and individualized support.

courses.title: Learning Support for Statistical Reasoning
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 credits. Total 3 hours per week. Corequisite: MTH 155
courses.description: Provides support to ensure success for students co-enrolled in Statistical Reasoning (MTH 155). Course will review foundational topics through direct instruction, guided practice, and individualized support.

courses.title: Intermediate Algebra
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Covers topics in algebra.

courses.title: Learning Support for Pre-Calculus
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Corequisite: MTH 161
courses.description: Provides support to ensure success for students co-enrolled in Pre-Calculus (MTH 161). Course will review foundational topics through direct instruction, guided practice, and individualized support.

courses.title: Blood Banking
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3-6 hours. Total 5-8 hours per week..
courses.description: Teaches fundamentals of blood grouping and typing, compatibility testing, antibody screening, component preparation, donor selection, and transfusion reactions and investigation.

courses.title: Introduction to Engineering Technology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces professional fields of engineering technology. Covers the work of the engineering technologist, professional ethics, division of industrial practice, and engineering problem solving with hand calculator and computer applications.

courses.title: Introduction to Engineering Technology I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces engineering technology. Provides historical background. Covers such topics as professional ethics; problem solving techniques involving forces, structures, materials, fluids, energy, and electricity and U.S. Customary and S.I. units, and unit conversions. Part I of II.

courses.title: Introduction to Engineering Technology II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces engineering technology. Provides historical background. Covers such topics as professional ethics; problem solving techniques involving forces, structures, materials, fluids, energy, and electricity and U.S. Customary and S.I. units, and unit conversions. Part II of II.

courses.title: Electronic Circuits and Instrumentation
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Designed for non-majors. Covers electronic circuits, devices, instrumentation and basic communications, DC and AC theory, introduction to power supplies, amplifiers, and measurement devices.

courses.title: Materials for Industry
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies the nature, structure, properties, and typical applications of metallic, polymeric, ceramic, and composite materials. Focuses on applications of materials as well as the behavior of materials subjected to external stresses. Addresses as required the earth's limited material resources, energy efficient materials, dependence on foreign sources of materials, material systems, thermal processing, and electronic-related materials.

courses.title: Processes of Industry
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Analyzes the processes of manufacturing products from materials for industry/engineering. Includes machining, casting, forming, molding, hot/cold working, chipless machining, and welding. Addresses quality assurance and inspection procedures.

courses.title: Materials and Processes of Industry
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies engineering materials and accompanying industrial manufacturing processes. Investigates nature of materials structure and properties from a design standpoint. Analyzes the effects of various processes on materials, and the processes themselves. Includes machining, casting, forming, molding, hot/cold working, cipless machining, and welding. Addresses quality assurance and inspection procedures.

courses.title: 3D Printing for Engineering Design
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours, Laboratory 3 hours, Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides an overview of rapid technologies in Additive Manufacturing that are high productivity tools designed to cut lead times, reduce time to market, increase the quality of the product, and improve collaboration within the organization.

courses.title: Mechanics I - Statics for Engineering Technology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches Newton's laws, resultants and equilibrium of force systems, trusses and frames, determination of centroids, and distributed loads and moments of inertia. Introduces dry friction and force systems in space.

courses.title: Mechanics II - Strength of Mat. for Eng. Tech
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches the concepts of stress and strain. Provides an analysis of stresses and deformations in loaded members, connectors, shafts, beams, columns, and combined stress.

courses.title: Mechanics III - Dynamics for Engineering Tech
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on rigid body mechanics including Kinetics, Kinematics, and applications to machine elements.

courses.title: Mechanics Laboratory
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 2 hours per week.
courses.description: Analyzes tension, compression, torsion, bending, fatigue, impact strength, and hardness of materials. Addresses static and dynamic stresses and strains. Provides for statistical evaluation of data. Includes experiments and/or demonstrations.

courses.title: Mechanisms
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Laboratory 2-4 hours. Total 3-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies the purpose and actions of cams, gear trains, levers, and other mechanical devices used to transmit control. Focuses on motions, linkages, velocities, and acceleration of points within a link mechanism; layout method for designing cams and gear grain. Requires preparation of weekly laboratory reports.

courses.title: Basic Fluid Mechanics - Hydraulics/Pneumatics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 4-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces theory, operation and maintenance of hydraulic/ pneumatics devices and systems. Emphasizes the properties of fluids, fluid flow, fluid statics, and the application of Bernoulli's equation.

courses.title: Applied Hydraulics and Pneumatics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-3 hours. Laboratory 1-3 hours. Total 2-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces hydraulic and pneumatic systems found in construction equipment, road vehicles, and farm equipment. Includes the basic theory, construction, maintenance and repair of hydraulic and pneumatic power systems.

courses.title: Applied Hydraulics, Pneumatics and Hydrostatics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches fluid power system design, operation, testing, maintenance and repair. Includes reservoirs, pump connecting valves, cylinders, pressure regulating valves, flow control valves, hydraulic motors, and introduction to basic hydrostatic hydraulic systems.

courses.title: Machine Design
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 1-2 hours. Total 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies the design of machine elements for producing and transmitting power. Includes additional material in statics, strength of materials, dynamics, engineering materials and industrial processes, including lubrication and friction. Emphasizes graphical kinematics of mechanisms, and discusses analytical design of machine components. Requires preparation of weekly laboratory reports.

courses.title: Machine Design I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours. Laboratory 1-3 hours. Total 4-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces analytical design of bearings, clutches, coupling, brakes, springs, gearing systems, and power shafting. Emphasizes methods of construction, machine parts and specifications of materials, and manufacturing processes. Part I of II.

courses.title: Machine Design II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours. Laboratory 1-3 hours. Total 4-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces analytical design of bearings, clutches, coupling, brakes, springs, gearing systems, and power shafting. Emphasizes methods of construction, machine parts and specifications of materials, and manufacturing processes. Part II of II.

courses.title: Fluid Mechanics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies properties of fluids and fluid flow, Bernoulli's theorem, measuring devices, viscosity and dimensional analysis. Emphasizes fluid statics, flow in pipes and channels, and pumps.

courses.title: Applications of Fluid Mechanics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches theory of hydraulic and pneumatic circuits including motors, controls, actuators, valves, plumbing, accumulators, reservoirs, pumps, compressors, and filters.

courses.title: Coordinated Internship
courses.contact_hours: Credit/practice ratio not to exceed 1:5 hours. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Supervises on-the-job training in selected business, industrial or service firms coordinated by the college.

courses.title: Topics In
courses.contact_hours: May be used also for special honors courses. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Provides an opportunity to explore topical areas of interest to or needed by students.

courses.title: Cooperative Education
courses.contact_hours: Credit/work ratio not to exceed 1:5 hours. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Supervises in on-the-job training for pay in approved business, industrial and service firms, coordinated by the college's cooperative education office. Is applicable to all occupational- technical curricula at the discretion of the college.

courses.title: Seminar and Project
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Requires completion of a project or research report related to the student's occupational objectives and a study of approaches to the selection and pursuit of career opportunities in the field.

courses.title: Supervised Study
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.

courses.title: Seminar and Project
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Requires completion of a project or research report related to the student's occupational objectives and a study of approaches to the selection and pursuit of career opportunities in the field.

courses.title: Supervised Study
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Assigns problems for independent study incorporating previous instruction and supervised by the instructor.

courses.title: Principles of Marketing
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents principles, methods, and problems involved in marketing to consumers and organizational buyers. Discusses problems and policies connected with distribution and sale of products, pricing, promotion, and buyer motivation. Examines variations of marketing research, legal, social, ethical, e-commerce, and international considerations in marketing.

courses.title: Principles of Selling
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents a fundamental, skills-based approach to selling and relationship building. Emphasizes learning effective interpersonal communication skills in all areas of the sales process through skill-building activities. Examines entry-level sales careers in retailing, wholesaling, services and industrial selling.

courses.title: Introduction to Marketing
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces students to the discipline of marketing and the need to create customer value and relationships in the marketplace. Presents an overview of the marketing principles and management strategies, along with the analytical tools used by organizations in the creation of a marketing plan.

courses.title: Sports, Entertainment, and Recreation Marketing
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Builds on the principles of marketing to introduce the more specific importance and specialization of Sports, Entertainment and Recreation (SER) marketing. Emphasizes the SER industries as they relate to the economics, business structure, product development, branding, pricing strategies, distribution strategies, integrated communications, ethics, and research.

courses.title: Retail Organization and Management
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines the organization of the retail establishment to accomplish its goals in an effective and efficient manner. Includes study of site location, internal layout, store operations, and security. Examines the retailing mix, the buying or procurement process, pricing, and selling. Studies retail advertising, promotion, and publicity as a coordinated effort to increase store traffic.

courses.title: Principles of Advertising
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Emphasizes the role of advertising in the marketing of goods, services, and ideas. Discusses the different uses of advertising; types of media; how advertising is created; agency functions; and legal, social, and economic aspects of the industry. Introduces advertising display, copy and art work preparation, printing and selection of media.

courses.title: Merchandise Buying and Control
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies the merchandising cycle. Explores techniques used in the development of buying resources, merchandising plans, model stock, unit control, and inventory systems. Highlights merchandise selection, policy pricing strategies, and inventory control methods.

courses.title: Promotion
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents an overview of integrated marketing communications through advertising, public relations, personal selling and sales promotion. Focuses on coordinating these activities into an effective campaign to promote sales for a particular product, business, institution or industry.

courses.title: Marketing Management
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Expands knowledge of marketing through case studies. Focuses on how marketing strategies are planned and utilized in the market place to accomplish the goals of the organization.

courses.title: Consumer Behavior
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines the various influences affecting consumer buying behavior before, during, and after product purchases. Describes personal, societal, cultural, environmental, group, and economic determinants on consumer buying.

courses.title: International Marketing
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines the role of global business as well as the environments in which they operate. Covers marketing strategies as they apply to global markets and contrasts them with domestic strategies.

courses.title: Principles of E-Commerce
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies on-line business strategies, and the hardware and software tools necessary for Internet commerce. Includes the identification of appropriate target segments, the development of product opportunities, pricing structures, distribution channels and execution of marketing strategies.

courses.title: Social Media Marketing
courses.contact_hours: Credit Hours: 3, Lecture Hours: 3, Lab Hours: 0, Total Contact Hours: 3
courses.description: Surveys the use of social networks and online communities such as blogs, wikis, virtual events that allow companies to expand their interaction with customers and develop relationships with collaborative communities. Emphasizes the ongoing transformation of the way companies adjust their marketing plans to improve interaction with customers online.

courses.title: Current Issues in Marketing
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Serves as a capstone course for marketing majors. Provides an integrated perspective of current issues and practices in marketing. Explores contemporary issues and practices in a highly participatory classroom environment.

courses.title: Basic Technical Mathematics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides a foundation in mathematics with emphasis in arithmetic, unit conversion, basic algebra, geometry and trigonometry. This course is intended for CTE programs.

courses.title: Fundamentals of Reasoning
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents elementary concepts of algebra, linear graphing, financial literacy, descriptive statistics, and measurement & geometry. Based on college programs being supported by this course, colleges may opt to add additional topics such as logic or trigonometry. This course is intended for occupational/technical programs.

courses.title: Technical Mathematics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents algebra through unit conversion, trigonometry, vectors, geometry, and complex numbers. This course is intended for CTE programs.

courses.title: Business Mathematics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides instruction, review, and drill in percentage, cash and trade discounts, mark-up, payroll, sales, property and other taxes, simple and compound interest, bank discounts, loans, investments, and annuities. This course is intended for occupational/technical programs.

courses.title: Quantitative Reasoning
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents topics in proportional reasoning, modeling, financial literacy and validity studies (logic and set theory). Focuses on the process of taking a real-world situation, identifying the mathematical foundation needed to address the problem, solving the problem and applying what is learned to the original situation. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Statistical Reasoning
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours, Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents elementary statistical methods and concepts including visual data presentation, descriptive statistics, probability, estimation, hypothesis testing, correlation and linear regression. Emphasis is placed on the development of statistical thinking, simulation, and the use of statistical software. Credit will not be awarded for both MTH 155 : Statistical Reasoning and MTH 245 : Statistics I or equivalent. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: PreCalculus I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents topics in power, polynomial, rational, exponential, and logarithmic functions, and systems of equations and inequalities. Credit will not be awarded for both MTH 161 : Precalculus I and MTH 167 : Precalculus with Trigonometry or equivalent. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: PreCalculus II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisites: Placement or completion of MTH 161 : Precalculus I or equivalent with a grade of C or better
courses.description: Presents trigonometry, trigonometric applications including Law of Sines and Cosines and an introduction to conics. Credit will not be awarded for both MTH 162 : Precalculus II and MTH 167 : Precalculus with Trigonometry or equivalent. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Finite Math
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents topics in systems of equations, matrices, linear programming, mathematics of finance, counting theory, probability, and Markov Chains. Emphasis is placed on the development of mathematical skills that are then applied to business applications and models.

courses.title: PreCalculus with Trigonometry
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 5 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents topics in power, polynomial, rational, exponential, and logarithmic functions, systems of equations, trigonometry, and trigonometric applications, including Law of Sines and Cosines, and an introduction to conics. Credit will not be awarded for both MTH 167 : Precalculus with Trigonometry and MTH 161 /MTH 162: Precalculus I and II or equivalent. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Studies In
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Covers new content not covered in existing courses in the discipline. Allows instructor to explore content and instructional methods to assess the course's viability as a permanent offering.

courses.title: Topics In
courses.contact_hours: May be used also for special honors courses. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.

courses.title: Seminar and Project

courses.title: Supervised Study
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Assigns problems for independent study incorporating previous instruction and supervised by the instructor.

courses.title: Statistics I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: Completion of MTH 154 or MTH 161 or equivalent with a grade of C or better.
courses.description: Presents an overview of statistics, including descriptive statistics, elementary probability, probability distributions, estimation, hypothesis testing, correlation, and linear regression. Credit will not be awarded for both MTH 155 and MTH 245 or equivalent in the same academic plan. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Statistics II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: Completion of MTH 245 or equivalent with a grade of C or better.
courses.description: Continues the study of estimation and hypothesis testing with emphasis on advanced regression topics, experimental design, analysis of variance, chi-square tests and non-parametric methods.

courses.title: Applied Calculus I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: Completion of MTH 161 or equivalent with a grade of C or better.
courses.description: Introduces limits, continuity, differentiation and integration of algebraic, exponential and logarithmic functions, and techniques of integration with an emphasis on applications in business, social sciences and life sciences. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Applied Calculus II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: Completion of MTH 261 or equivalent with a grade of C or better.
courses.description: Covers techniques of integration, an introduction to differential equations and multivariable calculus, with an emphasis throughout on applications in business, social sciences and life sciences.

courses.title: Calculus I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4 hours. Total 4 hours per week. Prerequisite: Completion of MTH 167 or MTH 161 /162 or equivalent with a grade of C or better.
courses.description: Presents concepts of limits, derivatives, differentiation of various types of functions and use of differentiation rules, application of differentiation, antiderivatives, integrals and applications of integration. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Calculus II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4 hours. Total 4 hours per week. Prerequisite: Completion of MTH 263 or equivalent with a grade of C or better.
courses.description: Continues the study of calculus of algebraic and transcendental functions including rectangular, polar, and parametric graphing, indefinite and definite integrals, methods of integration, and power series along with applications. Features instruction for mathematical, physical and engineering science programs. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Calculus III
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4 hours. Total 4 hours per week. Prerequisite: Completion of MTH 264 : Calculus II or equivalent with a grade of C or better
courses.description: Focuses on extending the concepts of function, limit, continuity, derivative, integral and vector from the plane to the three dimensional space. Covers topics including vector functions, multivariate functions, partial derivatives, multiple integrals and an introduction to vector calculus. Features instruction for mathematical, physical and engineering science programs.

courses.title: Linear Algebra
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: Completion of MTH 263 or equivalent with a grade of B or better or MTH 264 or equivalent with a grade of C or better.
courses.description: Covers matrices, vector spaces, determinants, solutions of systems of linear equations, basis and dimension, eigenvalues, and eigenvectors. Features instruction for mathematical, physical and engineering science programs.

courses.title: Differential Equations
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: Completion of MTH 264 or equivalent with a grade of C or better.
courses.description: Introduces ordinary differential equations. Includes first order differential equations, second and higher order ordinary differential equations with applications and numerical methods.

courses.title: Probability and Statistics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: Completion of MTH 264 with a grade of C or better or equivalent.
courses.description: Presents basic concepts of probability, discrete and continuous random variables, and probability distributions. Presents sampling distributions and the Central Limit Theorem, properties of point estimates and methods of estimation, confidence intervals, hypothesis testing, linear models and estimation by least squares, and analysis of variance.

courses.title: Discrete Mathematics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 credits. Total 3 credits per week. Prerequisite: Completion of MTH 263 with a grade of C or better or equivalent.
courses.description: Presents topics in sets, counting, graphs, logic, proofs, functions, relations, mathematical induction, Boolean Algebra, and recurrence relations.

courses.title: Supervised Study
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Assigns problems for independent study incorporating previous instruction and supervised by the instructor.

courses.title: Fundamentals of Music
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides the ability to read and identify basic fundamentals of music notation. Teaches major and minor scales, chords and basic harmonic progressions. Covers basic ear training and keyboard exercises. This is a UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Music Theory I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Discusses elements of musical construction of scales, intervals, triads, and chord progressions. Develops ability to sing at sight and write from dictation. Introduces the analysis of the Bach chorale style. Expands facility with harmonic dictation and enables the student to use these techniques at the keyboard. Part I of II.

courses.title: Music Theory II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Discusses elements of musical construction of scales, intervals, triads, and chord progressions. Develops ability to sing at sight and write from dictation. Introduces the analysis of the Bach chorale style. Expands facility with harmonic dictation and enables the student to use these techniques at the keyboard. Part II of II.

courses.title: Music in Society
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Explores the language of music through an introduction to basic elements, forms and styles across time. Acquaints students with composers' lives and influential creative individualities, discovering representative works and milestones in western society. Develops techniques for listening analytically and critically. Reviews historical development and significance of art music within the context of evolving societal structures. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: American Music
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents the development of music in America from early colonists to the present, in light of philosophical, political, geographical, and sociological developments.

courses.title: Overview of the Recording Industry
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour per week. Prerequisite: divisional approval.
courses.description: Introduces and surveys employment opportunities in the commercial music industry. Assists students in defining their professional goals.

courses.title: Class Voice I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the many aspects of singing from the physical act through the aesthetic experience. The course is designed for the beginning singer who desires vocal improvement, and for the voice major as an addition to and extension of skills and knowledge necessary for artistic development. Introduces appropriate repertoire. Part I of II.

courses.title: Class Voice II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the many aspects of singing from the physical act through the aesthetic experience. The course is designed for the beginning singer who desires vocal improvement, and for the voice major as an addition to and extension of skills and knowledge necessary for artistic development. Introduces appropriate repertoire. Part II of II.

courses.title: Recording Systems Services I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week. Prerequisite: divisional approval.
courses.description: Introduces the principles of recording systems and recording system designs. Provides the student with theoretical and practical site locations. Includes the study of sound studio design and construction, production costs, and retail distribution. Part I of II.

courses.title: Jazz Ensemble
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 0, Laboratory 3-6 hours. Total 3-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Consists of performance from Standard Jazz and American Songbook Repertoires, including study of ensemble techniques, interpretation, and improvisation. Divisional approval required. May be repeated for credit.

courses.title: Applied Music-Voice
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 4-8 hours per week. Total 4-8 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches singing, proper breath control, diction, and development of tone. Studies the standard vocal repertoire. Private lessons are available for either 1 or 2 hours of credit per semester. The length of the lessons will be 1/2 hour for 1 hour credit and 1 hour for 2 hours credit per semester. All courses in applied music may be repeated for a total of 8 hours for the major and 4 hours for the minor. One or two half-hour lessons per week. Four to eight hours practice required.

courses.title: Chorus Ensemble
courses.contact_hours: Credits 1 - 2. Laboratory 3-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Ensemble consists of performance from the standard repertoires, including study of ensemble techniques and interpretation. May be repeated for credit.

courses.title: Small Vocal Ensemble
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 3-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Ensemble consist of performance from the standard repertoires, including study of ensemble techniques and interpretation. Divisional approval required. May be repeated for credit.

courses.title: Introduction to Recording Techniques
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces students to the theory of and practices in digital audio. Describes basic background of the history of audio, culminating with hands-on operation of a digital audio workstation (DAW). The student is not expected to have any previous musical experience.

courses.title: Class Piano I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Offers the beginning piano student activities in learning musical notation, in accomplishing sight reading skills, and in mastering techniques of keyboard playing. Presents appropriate literature. Open to all students and may be used to fulfill applied minor instrument requirement for music major. Part I of II.

courses.title: Class Piano II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Offers the beginning piano student activities in learning musical notation, in accomplishing sight reading skills, and in mastering techniques of keyboard playing. Presents appropriate literature. Open to all students and may be used to fulfill applied minor instrument requirement for music major. Part II of II.

courses.title: Applied Music - Keyboard
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 4-8 hours. Total 4-8 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches piano, organ, harpsichord, or synthesizer. Studies the standard repertoire. Private lessons are available for either 1 or 2 hours of credit per semester. The length of the lessons will be 1/2 hour for 1 hour credit and 1 hour for 2 hours credit per semester. All courses in applied music may be repeated for a total of 8 hours for the major and 4 hours for the minor. 1-2 half-hour lessons per week, 4-8 hours practice (laboratory) required.

courses.title: Orchestra Ensemble
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 3-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Ensemble consist of performance from the standard repertoires, including study of ensemble techniques and interpretation. Divisional approval required. May be repeated for credit.

courses.title: Band Ensemble
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 3-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Ensemble consists of performance from the standard repertoires, including study of ensemble techniques and interpretation. Divisional approval required. May be repeated for credit.

courses.title: Applied Music - Woodwinds
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 4-8 hours per week. Total 4-8 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches fundamentals of the woodwind instruments. Studies the standard repertoire. Private lessons are available for either 1 or 2 hours of credit per semester. The length of the lessons will be 1/2 hour for 1 hour credit and 1 hour for 2 hours credit per semester. All courses in applied music may be repeated for a total of 8 hours for the major and 4 hours for the minor. 1-2 half-hour lessons per week, 4-8 hours practice (laboratory) required.

courses.title: Sound Studio Design
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week. Prerequisite: divisional approval.
courses.description: Introduces the theory and practice of sound studio design. Provides a basic understanding of acoustics and the acoustical properties of construction materials. Allows the student practical opportunities in designing sound studios.

courses.title: Recording Studio Electronics: Theory and Maintenance
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week. Prerequisite: divisional approval.
courses.description: Introduces the practices used in maintaining professional recording equipment and basic electronic theory used within the recording industry. Provides the skills and knowledge necessary to perform routine maintenance and to repair recording and related equipment. Designed to prepare the student for position as entry-level technician or apprentice recording engineer.

courses.title: Improvisational Techniques
courses.contact_hours: Credits 3. Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the principles of improvisation using harmonic structures and progressions from the period of common practice. Includes listening to and performing music of the standard jazz and popular repertoire. Develops performance skills utilizing specific improvisational devices employed in different historical periods.

courses.title: Guitar Theory and Practice I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies the fundamentals of sound production, music theory, and harmony as they apply to guitar. Builds proficiency in both the techniques of playing the guitar and in the application of music fundamentals to these techniques. Presents different types of guitars and related instruments. Emphasizes music as entertainment and as a communication skill. Part I of II.

courses.title: Guitar Theory and Practice II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies the fundamentals of sound production, music theory, and harmony as they apply to guitar. Builds proficiency in both the techniques of playing the guitar and in the application of music fundamentals to these techniques. Presents different types of guitars and related instruments. Emphasizes music as entertainment and as a communication skill. Part II of II.

courses.title: Applied Music - Strings
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 4-8 hours per week. Total 4-8 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches fundamentals of string instruments, harp, or guitar. Studies the standard repertoire. Private lessons are available for either 1 or 2 hours of credit per semester. The length of the lessons will be 1/2 hour for 1 hour credit and 1 hour for 2 hours credit per semester. All courses in applied music may be repeated for a total of 8 hours for the major and 4 hours for the minor. 1-2 half-hour lessons per week, 4-8 hours practice (laboratory) required.

courses.title: Beginning Mandolin
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours, Laboratory 2 hours per week.
courses.description: An introductory level course on the history of the mandolin, regional musicians, influences, and performance with emphasis on the old time styles found in the central Appalachian region. Classroom instruction will include lecture, demonstrations, assignments, reports, and quizzes. Student practice will be required outside of classroom hours.

courses.title: Applied Music - Brass
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 4-8 hours per week. Total 4-8 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches fundamentals of brass instruments. Studies the standard repertoire. Private lessons are available for either 1 or 2 hours of credit per semester. The length of the lessons will be 1/2 hour for 1 hour credit and 1 hour for 2 hours credit per semester. All courses in applied music may be repeated for a total of 8 hours for the major and 4 hours for the minor. 1-2 half-hour lessons per week, 4-8 hours practice (laboratory) required.

courses.title: Music Copyright Law
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour per week. Prerequisite: divisional approval.
courses.description: Introduces the legal problems and normal conventions practiced within the commercial music industry. Provides a basic understanding of national and international music copyright laws.

courses.title: Applied Music - Percussion
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 4-8 hours per week. Total 4-8 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches fundamentals of percussion instruments. Studies the standard repertoire. Private lessons are available for either 1 or 2 hours of credit per semester. The length of the lessons will be 1/2 hour for 1 hour credit and 1 hour for 2 hours credit per semester. All courses in applied music may be repeated for a total of 8 hours for the major and 4 hours for the minor. 1-2 half-hour lessons per week, 4-8 hours practice (laboratory) required.
