courses.title: Fundamentals of Physical Activity I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 0-1 hours. Laboratory 2-4 hours. Total 2-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents principles underlying the components of physical fitness. Utilizes conditioning activities involving cardiovascular strength and endurance, respiratory efficiency, muscular strength, and flexibility. May include fitness assessment, nutrition and weight control information, and concepts of wellness. Part I of II.

courses.title: Fundamentals of Physical Activity II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 0-1 hours. Laboratory 2-4 hours. Total 2-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents principles underlying the components of physical fitness. Utilizes conditioning activities involving cardiovascular strength and endurance, respiratory efficiency, muscular strength, and flexibility. May include fitness assessment, nutrition and weight control information, and concepts of wellness. Part II of II.

courses.title: Aerobic Fitness I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 0-1 hours. Laboratory 2-4 hours. Total 2-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Develops cardiovascular fitness though activities designed to elevate and sustain heart rates appropriate to age and physical condition. Part I of II.

courses.title: Aerobic Fitness II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 0-1 hours. Laboratory 2-4 hours. Total 2-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Develops cardiovascular fitness though activities designed to elevate and sustain heart rates appropriate to age and physical condition. Part II of II.

courses.title: Exercise and Nutrition I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 0-1 hours. Laboratory 2-4 hours. Total 2-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides for the study and application of fitness and wellness and their relationship to a healthy lifestyle. Defines fitness and wellness, evaluates the student's level of fitness and wellness. Students will incorporate physical fitness and wellness into the course and daily living. A personal fitness/wellness plan is required for the 2 credit course. Part I of II.

courses.title: Exercise and Nutrition II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 0-1 hours. Laboratory 2-4 hours. Total 2-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides for the study and application of fitness and wellness and their relationship to a healthy lifestyle. Defines fitness and wellness, evaluates the student's level of fitness and wellness. Students will incorporate physical fitness and wellness into the course and daily living. A personal fitness/wellness plan is required for the 2 credit course. Part I of II.

courses.title: Yoga
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 0-1 hours. Laboratory 2-4 hours. Total 2-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on the forms of yoga training emphasizing flexibility.

courses.title: Weight Training I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 0-1 hours. Laboratory 2-4 hours. Total 2-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on muscular strength and endurance training through individualized workout programs. Teaches appropriate use of weight training equipment. Part I of II.

courses.title: Weight Training II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 0-1 hours. Laboratory 2-4 hours. Total 2-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on muscular strength and endurance training through individualized workout programs. Teaches appropriate use of weight training equipment. Part II of II.

courses.title: Lifetime Fitness and Wellness
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 0-1 hours. Laboratory 2-4 hours. Total 2-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides a study of fitness and wellness and their relationship to a healthy lifestyle. Defines fitness and wellness, evaluates the student's level of fitness and wellness, and motivates the student to incorporate physical fitness and wellness into daily living. A personal fitness/wellness plan is required for the 2-credit course.

courses.title: Fitness Walking
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 2 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches content and skills needed to design, implement, and evaluate an individualized program of walking, based upon fitness level.

courses.title: Yoga II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 0-1 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 2-3 hours per week. Prerequisite: PED 109 .
courses.description: Focuses on the forms of yoga training emphasizing flexibility.

courses.title: Archery
courses.contact_hours: Lecture
courses.description: Teaches skills and techniques of target archery. Focuses on use and maintenance of equipment, terminology, and safety.

courses.title: Self-Defense
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 0-1 hours. Laboratory 2-4 hours. Total 2-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines history, techniques, and movements associated with self-defense. Introduces the skills and methods of self- defense emphasizing mental and physical discipline.

courses.title: Volleyball
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 0-1hours. Laboratory 2-4 hours. Total 2-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces skills, techniques, strategies, rules, and scoring.

courses.title: Basic Personal Trainer Preparation
courses.contact_hours: 3 credit hours. 2 lecture hours. 2 lab hours. 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the skills and knowledge required to become a personal trainer. Includes the principles of individual weight management, personal wellness, and the skills necessary for the creation of a fitness program for potential clients.

courses.title: Ballroom Dance I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 0-1 hours. Laboratory 2-4 hours. Total 2-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents the basic step patterns, rhythmic patterns, and positions in ballroom dance. Includes techniques based upon traditional steps with basic choreographic patterns. Part I of II.

courses.title: Ballroom Dance II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 0-1 hours. Laboratory 2-4 hours. Total 2-4hours per week.
courses.description: Presents the basic step patterns, rhythmic patterns, and positions in ballroom dance. Includes techniques based upon traditional steps with basic choreographic patterns. Part II of II.

courses.title: Rock Climbing and Rappelling
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 0-1hours. Laboratory 2-4 hours. Total 2-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents techniques and skills of climbing and rappelling with emphasis on safety, equipment, skills in knot typing, terminology and physical conditioning.

courses.title: Outdoor Adventures I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 0-1 hours. Laboratory 2-4 hours. Total 2-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces outdoor adventure activities with emphasis on basic skills, preparation, personal and group safety, equipment selection and use, ecology, and field experience. Part I of II.

courses.title: Backpacking
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 0-1 hours. Laboratory 2-4 hours. Total 2-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on the preparation for backpacking trip, equipment and clothing selection, personal and group safety, ecology, and physical conditioning. Includes field experience.

courses.title: Freshwater Fishing
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 0-1 hours. Laboratory 2-4 hours. Total 2-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches freshwater fishing techniques including spinning, bait casting and fly casting. Presents selection and care of equipment, fish habits, conservation, and safety.

courses.title: Topics In
courses.contact_hours: May be used also for special honors courses. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Provides an opportunity to explore topical areas of interest to or needed by students.

courses.title: Seminar and Project
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Requires completion of a project or research report related to the student's occupational objectives and a study of approaches to the selection and pursuit of career opportunities in the field.

courses.title: Supervised Study
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Assigns problems for independent study incorporating previous instruction and supervised by the instructor.

courses.title: Sports Appreciation
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on the history, trends, rules, methods, strategy, and terminology of selected sports activities. Provides student awareness as a spectator and/or participant.

courses.title: Introduction to Philosophy
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents an introduction to philosophical problems and perspectives with emphasis on the systematic questioning of basic assumptions about meaning, knowledge, reality, and values. The assignments in the course require college-level reading fluency and coherent communication through written reports. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Logic
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces inductive and deductive reasoning, with an emphasis on common errors and fallacies. The assignments in the course require college-level reading fluency and coherent communication through written reports. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Topics In
courses.contact_hours: May be used also for special honors courses. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Provides an opportunity to explore topical areas of interest to or needed by students.

courses.title: Seminar and Project
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Requires completion of a project or research report related to the student's occupational objectives and a study of approaches to the selection and pursuit of career opportunities in the field.

courses.title: Supervised Study
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Assigns problems for independent study incorporating previous instruction and supervised by the instructor.

courses.title: The History of Western Philosophy
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Offers a historical survey of major philosophers from the ancient Greeks to the modern era. The assignments in this course require the ability to write at the college level, read college-level philosophical texts, and understand and apply philosophical concepts with complex meanings.

courses.title: Ethics and Society
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides a systematic study of representative ethical concepts and theories and discusses their application to concrete moral dilemmas and social issues and problems. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Biomedical Ethics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces medical ethics with an emphasis on practical moral issues faced by professionals in medicine, public health and related fields. Explores major theories, concepts and terminology in the field of bioethics.

courses.title: Topics In
courses.contact_hours: May be used also for special honors courses. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Provides an opportunity to explore topical areas of interest to or needed by students.

courses.title: Introduction to Photography
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces principles of photography with outside shooting assignments related to lecture topics.

courses.title: Photography I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Laboratory 4 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches principles of photography and fundamental camera techniques. Requires outside shooting and lab work. Part I of II.

courses.title: Photography II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches principles of photography and fundamental camera techniques. Requires outside shooting and lab work. Part II of II.

courses.title: Black and White Darkroom Photography I
courses.contact_hours: 3 Credits. Lecture 2 hours per week, Lab 2 hours per week, Total 4 contact hours per week.
courses.description: Highlights principles of photography including camera operation and darkroom procedures. Focuses on black and white photography. Requires outside shooting and lab work.

courses.title: Basic Photography
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-4 hours. Laboratory 1-3 hours. Total 3-7 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies fundamental techniques of the camera and its expressive possibilities.

courses.title: History of Photography
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Surveys important photographers, processes, and historical influences of the nineteenth and twentieth centuries.

courses.title: Electronic Darkroom
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hour. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches students to create and manipulate digital photographs. Covers masking, color corrections, and merging of illustrations with photographs. Examines the ethical and property-rights issues which are raised in the manipulation of images.

courses.title: Introduction to Digital Photography
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces fundamental techniques of photography, including digital camera operation, postproduction, and printing. Includes technical and conceptual exercises, individual project development, and group critiques.

courses.title: Supervised Study
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Assigns problems for independent study incorporating previous instruction and supervised by the instructor.

courses.title: Advanced Photography I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week. Prerequisite: PHT 102 or equivalent.
courses.description: Provides weekly critiques of students' work. Centers on specific problems found in critiques. Includes working procedures and critical skills in looking at photographs. Part I of II.

courses.title: Advanced Photography II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week. Prerequisite: PHT 102 or equivalent.
courses.description: Provides weekly critiques of students' work. Centers on specific problems found in critiques. Includes working procedures and critical skills in looking at photographs.Part II of II.

courses.title: Large Format Photography
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week. Prerequisite: PHT 102 or equivalent.
courses.description: Discusses 4x5 view camera techniques and controls, and sheet film processing. Demonstrates the image-making advantages of large format photography.

courses.title: Outdoor and Wildlife Photography
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches advanced wildlife, outdoor and nature photography. Covers topics such as flash, hyperfocal distance, and maximizing the cameras' digital potential.

courses.title: Studio Lighting I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines advanced lighting and camera techniques under controlled studio conditions. Includes view camera use, electronic flash, advanced lighting techniques, color temperature and filtration, and lighting ratios. Requires outside shooting. Part I of II.

courses.title: Studio Lighting II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week. Prerequisite: PHT 102 or equivalent.
courses.description: Examines advanced lighting and camera techniques under controlled studio conditions. Includes view camera use, electronic flash, advanced lighting techniques, color temperature and filtration, and lighting ratios. Requires outside shooting. Part II of II.

courses.title: Commercial Photography
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines advanced topics relating to commercial photography. Emphasizes advertising, portraiture, and commercial and public relations.

courses.title: Careers in Photography and Media
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces students of photography and video to a variety professional opportunities in the field. This is an advanced course for students who would like to know more about their options in staff and freelance work.

courses.title: Alternative Photographic Processes
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Laboratory 4 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Explores manipulated imagery including traditional and non- traditional processes such as non-silver and electronic imaging. Uses enlarged film negatives in order to investigate a variety of methods.

courses.title: Digital Photography II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches theory and practice of digital photography. Emphasizes use of digital cameras in studio and on location. Teaches advanced techniques of image editing. Provides training in digital image transmission from remote locations.

courses.title: Elements of Physics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Covers basic concepts of physics, including Newtonian mechanics, properties of matter, heat transfer, waves, fundamental behavior of gases, optics, ionizing radiation, and fundamentals of electricity and magnetism. The assignments in the course require college-level reading fluency, coherent written communication, application of arithmetic, exponents, and algebraic skills such as solving for an unknown variable in an equation, and finding the slope and intercept from the equation of a line. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Applied Physics I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Emphasizes application of topics such as precision measurement, statics, dynamics, energy, momentum, properties of matter, heat, sound, optics, and electricity and magnetism. Prerequisites high school algebra, geometry and trigonometry, or equivalent or divisional approval. Part I of II. This course applies to career/technical education (CTE) programs. PHY 100 serves both transfer and CTE programs.

courses.title: Astronomy: Solar System
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces astronomy of the solar system, including the Sun, planets, their satellites, and other solar system objects. Includes discussions of the development of astronomy through the ages, recent discoveries, and experience with the types of mathematical exercises and observational skills essential for an understanding of the fundamental principles of solar system astronomy. Assignments require fluency in arithmetic, unit conversion, basic algebra, geometry, and trigonometry. This course is cross-listed with NAS 131 . Credit will not be awarded for both.

courses.title: Astronomy: Stars and Galaxies
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces astronomy of the stars, including the Sun, celestial objects, stellar formation and death and cosmology, and the study of the universe as a whole. Includes discussions of the development of astronomy through the ages, recent discoveries and experience with the types of mathematical principles employed and the astronomical observational skills essential for an understanding of the fundamental principles of astronomy and cosmology. Assignments require fluency in arithmetic, unit conversion, basic algebra, geometry, and trigonometry. This course is cross-listed with NAS 132 . Credit will not be awarded for both.

courses.title: Elements of Astronomy
courses.contact_hours: 4 Credits. Lecture 3 hours. Lab 3 hours. Total 6 hours.
courses.description: Covers history of astronomy and its recent developments. Stresses the use of astronomical instruments and measuring techniques and includes the study and observation of the solar system, stars, and galaxies.

courses.title: General College Physics I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week. Prerequisite: MTH 161 or MTH 167 with a grade of C or better.
courses.description: Covers classical mechanics and thermodynamics. Includes kinematics, Newton's laws of motion, work, energy, momentum, rotational kinematics, dynamic and static equilibrium, elasticity, gravitation, fluids, simple harmonic motion, calorimetry, ideal gas law, and the laws of thermodynamics. Part I of II. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: General College Physics II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week. Prerequisite: PHY 201 with a grade of C or better and MTH 162 or MTH 167 with a grade of C or better.
courses.description: Covers waves, electromagnetism, optics, and modern physics. Includes mechanical waves, sound, electrostatics, Ohm's law and DC circuits, magnetic forces and magnetic fields, electromagnetic induction, ray optics, wave optics, and selected topics of modern physics. Part II of II. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: University Physics I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week. Prerequisites: MTH 263 with a grade of C or better.
courses.description: Covers classical mechanics and thermodynamics. Includes kinematics, Newton's laws of motion, work, energy, momentum, rotational kinematics, dynamics and static equilibrium, elasticity, gravitation, fluids, simple harmonic motion, calorimetry, ideal gas law, and the laws of thermodynamics. Part I of II. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: University Physics II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week. Prerequisites: PHY 241 with a grade of C or better and MTH 264 with a grade of C or better.
courses.description: Covers waves, electromagnetism and optics. Includes mechanical waves and sound, electrostatics, Ohm's law and DC circuits, magnetic forces and magnetic fields, electromagnetic induction, AC circuits, ray optics, and wave optics. Part II of II. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: U.S. Government and Politics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches the political structure, processes, institutions, and policymaking of the US national government. Focuses on the three branches of government, their interrelationships, and how they shape policy. Addresses federalism; civil liberties and civil rights; political socialization and participation; public opinion, the media; interest groups; political parties; elections; and policymaking. The assignments in the course require college-level reading fluency and coherent communication through written reports. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: State and Local Government and Politics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches structure, powers, and functions of state and local government in the United States as related to federalism; constitutionalism; elections; powers of legislative, executive, and judicial powers of state and local government; state-local-federal relations; fiscal matters; metropolitan issues; and policy issues, like health, education, criminal justice and welfare. The assignments in the course require college-level reading fluency and coherent communication through written reports.

courses.title: Introduction to Comparative Politics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Teach concepts and methods of comparative politics. Includes empirical analyses of domestic governmental, political, and societal institutions and norms of countries around the world. The assignments in the course require college-level reading fluency and coherent communication through written reports. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Introduction to Political and Democratic Theory
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents concepts of politics using political theory. Emphasizes the core thinkers and themes of political theory, with focus on concepts of justice, power, rights, liberty, and citizenship, within the context of differing conceptions of the state. Apply political theory as a method of analysis for analyzing current political events and problems. The assignments in the course require college-level reading fluency and coherent communication through written reports.

courses.title: Introduction to International Relations
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisites: ENG 111 or Department Consent
courses.description: Provides an introduction to the causes of international conflict and cooperation. Focuses on the modern state, diplomacy, war initiation, crisis bargaining, international terrorism, nuclear strategy, interstate economic relations, economic growth, international law, human rights, and environmental politics. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Trends in Practical Nursing
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour per week.
courses.description: Studies the role of the Licensed Practical Nurse. Covers legal aspects, organizations, and opportunities in practical nursing. Assists students in preparation for employment.

courses.title: Medical-Surgical Nursing I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies etiology, symptoms, prescribed treatment, and experiences in the nursing care of patients with selected disorders. Selects learning experiences to correlate related patient care with classroom instruction whenever possible. Provides observational experiences when available.

courses.title: Body Structure and Function
courses.contact_hours: Lecure 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies the structure and function of the body.

courses.title: Mental Health and Psychiatric Nursing
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours per week.
courses.description: Recognizes emotional needs of patients. Provides knowledge of the role that emotions play. Enables students to understand their own behavior as well as patient behavior.

courses.title: Nursing in Health Changes I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-4 hours. Laboratory 6-15 hours. Total 10-17 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on nursing situations and procedures necessary to assist individuals in meeting special needs related to human functions.

courses.title: Nursing in Health Changes II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4-6 hours. Laboratory 12-21 hours. Total 18-25 hours per week.
courses.description: Continues the focus on nursing situations and procedures necessary to assist individuals in meeting special needs related to human functions.

courses.title: Nursing in Health Changes III
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4-5 hours. Laboratory 9-15 hours. Total 14-19 hours per week.
courses.description: Continues the focus on nursing situations and procedures necessary to assist individuals in meeting special needs related to human functions.

courses.title: Pharmacology for Practical Nurses
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies history, classification, sources, effects, uses and legalities of drugs. Teaches problem solving skills used in medication administrations. Emphasizes major drug classes and specific agents within each class.

courses.title: Coordinated Internship
courses.contact_hours: Credit/practice ratio not to exceed 1:5 hours. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Supervises on-the-job training in selected business, industrial or service firms coordinated by the college.

courses.title: Principles of Applied Psychology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the general principles of psychology as they are applied to work, relationships, and growth. Includes perception, learning, development, motivation, emotion, therapy, communication, attitudes.

courses.title: Psychology of Personal Adjustment
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces psychological principles that contribute to well- adjusted personality. Considers the effects of stress and coping with the problems of everyday life.

courses.title: Psychology of Death and Dying
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on psychological aspects of death and dying. Teaches the meaning of death and ways of handling its personal and social implications. Includes psychological, sociological, cultural, and religious views of death.

courses.title: Human Relations
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the theory and practice of effective human relations. Increases understanding of self and others and interpersonal skills needed to be a competent and cooperative communicator.

courses.title: Psychology for Business and Industry
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on the application of psychology to interpersonal relations and the working environment. Includes topics such as group dynamics, motivation, employee-employer relationship, interpersonal communications. May include techniques for selection and supervision of personnel.

courses.title: Principles of Psychology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Surveys the basic concepts of psychology. Covers the scientific study of behavior and mental processes, research methods, biological bases of behavior, sensation and perception, developmental psychology, learning, memory, thinking, intelligence, personality, social psychology, and psychological disorders and treatment. The assignments in the course require college-level reading fluency and coherent communication through written reports. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Research Methodology for Behavioral Sciences
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisites: PSY 200 AND PSY 210 or departmental approval.
courses.description: Introduces the principles and processes of various research methods for applying the scientific method to understanding behavior. Includes preparation for and fundamental experience with designing, conducting, interpreting, and evaluating behavioral science research studies. Prepares students for creating APA-style research manuscripts to summarize research.

courses.title: Statistics for Behavioral Sciences
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the principles and processes of statistics within behavioral research. Emphasizes understanding and applying statistical tests to behavioral data. Stresses recognition and use of process, based upon knowledge and understanding, over mathematical derivation. Focuses on selection of appropriate statistics, their application, and correct decisions of interpretation within a behavioral research experience.

courses.title: Psychopathology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: PSY 200 or departmental approval.
courses.description: Explores historical views and current perspectives of psychopathology. Emphasizes major diagnostic categories and criteria, individual and social factors of maladaptive behavior, and types of treatments. Includes methods of clinical assessment and research strategies.

courses.title: Social Psychology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisites: PSY 200 or departmental consent.
courses.description: Examines individuals in social contexts, their social roles, group processes and intergroup relations. Acquaints students with a scientific understanding of how the presence of other people, interactions with other people, and other situational factors influence human thoughts and behaviors. The assignments in the course require college-level reading, analysis of scholarly studies, and coherent communication through written reports (including the production of at least one APA-formatted individual writing assignment).

courses.title: Introduction to Behavior Modification
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies the history of behaviorism and the principles and applications of behavior modification. Emphasizes observation and application of behavior modification principles.

courses.title: Theories of Personality
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: PSY 200 or equivalent
courses.description: Studies the major personality theories and their applications. Includes psychodynamic, behavioral, cognitive, and humanistic perspectives.

courses.title: Introduction to Counselling Relationships
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces counseling theories and provides opportunity for their application through role-playing and supervised paraprofessional counseling experiences. Prerequisite Divisional Approval.

courses.title: Developmental Psychology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Traces development in context from pre-conception to death, including the physical, cognitive, and psychosocial domains. Examines methods of scientific inquiry as they apply to lifespan development. Addresses the interrelatedness of developmental domains, as well as the interdependent influences of environment and biology. Students majoring in or considering a major in Psychology should complete PSY 200 prior to PSY 230 .

courses.title: Life Span Human Development I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Investigates human behavior through the life cycle. Describes physical, cognitive, and psycho-social aspects of human development from conception to death. Part I of II.

courses.title: Life Span Human Development II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Investigates human behavior through the life cycle. Describes physical, cognitive, and psycho-social aspects of human development from conception to death. Part II of II.

courses.title: Child Psychology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies development of the child from conception to adolescence. Investigates physical, intellectual, social and emotional factors involved in the child's growth.

courses.title: Adolescent Psychology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies development of the adolescent. Investigates physical, intellectual, social, and emotional factors of the individual from late childhood to early adulthood.

courses.title: Adult Psychology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies development of the adult personality. Investigates physical, intellectual, social, and emotional aspects of aging from early adulthood to death.

courses.title: Psychological Aspects of Criminal Behavior
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week. Prerequisites: PSY 125 , PSY 200 , PSY 201 , PSY 202 or divisional approval.
courses.description: Studies psychology of criminal behavior. Includes topics such as violent and non-violent crime, sexual offenses, insanity, addiction, white collar crime, and other deviant behaviors. Provides a background for law enforcement occupations.

courses.title: Psychology of Human Sexuality
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week. Prerequisites: PSY 200 , PSY 201 or PSY 202 .
courses.description: Focuses on scientific investigation of human sexuality and psychological and social implications of such research. Considers socio-cultural influences, the physiology and psychology of sexual response patterns, sexual dysfunctions, and development of relationships.

courses.title: Principles of Real Estate
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines practical applications of real estate principles. Includes a study of titles, estates, land descriptions, contracts, legal instruments and concepts, real estate mathematics, financing, agency, appraisal, fair housing, and management of real estate.

courses.title: Seminar and Project
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Requires completion of a project or research report related to the student's occupational objectives and a study of approaches to the selection and pursuit of career opportunities in the field.

courses.title: Supervised Study
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Assigns problems for independent study incorporating previous instruction and supervised by the instructor.

courses.title: Supervised Study
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Assigns problems for independent study incorporating previous instruction and supervised by the instructor.

courses.title: Introduction to the Study of Religion
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Explores the idea of religion (as a general category), how to study religion in an academic context, and common elements across most religions such as beliefs, practices, values, community, spiritual experience, symbolism, and narrative. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Seminar and Project
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Requires completion of a project or research report related to the student's occupational objectives and a study of approaches to the selection and pursuit of career opportunities in the field.

courses.title: Supervised Study
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Assigns problems for independent study incorporating previous instruction and supervised by the instructor.

courses.title: Survey of the Old Testament
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Surveys books of the Old Testament, with emphasis on prophetic historical books. Examines the historical and geographical setting and place of the Israelites in the ancient Middle East as background to the writings.

courses.title: Survey of the New Testament
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Surveys books of the New Testament, with special attention upon placing the writings within their historical and geographical setting.

courses.title: New Testament and Early Christianity
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Surveys the history, literature, and theology of early Christianity in the light of the New Testament.

courses.title: Life and Letters of Paul
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies the journeys and religious thought of the apostle Paul.

courses.title: Selected Topics in Biblical Studies
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines a selected body of literature, a specific book of the Bible, or a pervasive theme.

courses.title: Religions of the World
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the major religions of the world: Judaism, Christianity, Islam, Hinduism, and Buddhism. Focuses on origins, history, basic beliefs, values, ethics, and practices. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Introduction to Islam
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies Islam in its historical, religious and political dimensions and assists in the understanding of its contemporary vitality and attraction as a faith, a culture and a way of life. Provides exposure to Muslim culture and religious practices through an experiential element.

courses.title: Religions in the U.S.
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Surveys various manifestations of religion in the American experience. Emphasizes concepts, problems, and issues of religious diversity and character of U.S. religious life. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Christianity
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines the origins and historical development of Christianity, its basic metaphysical and theological assumptions, its essential doctrines, and the present state of the church in the modern world.

courses.title: Seminar and Project
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Requires completion of a project or research report related to the student's occupational objectives and a study of approaches to the selection and pursuit of career opportunities in the field.

courses.title: Supervised Study
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Assigns problems for independent study incorporating previous instruction and supervised by the instructor.

courses.title: Beginning Russian I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces cultural awareness, listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills and emphasizes basic sentence structure. Part I of II. This is a UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Beginning Russian II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4 hours. Total 4 hours per week. Prerequisites: RUS 101 , or two years of successful completion of high school Russian, or demonstrated experiential learning, or by placement test, or equivalent.
courses.description: Develops the understanding, speaking, reading, and writing of Russian, and emphasizes the structure of the language. May include oral drill and practice. Part II of II. This is a UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Intermediate Russian I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4 hours. Total 4 hours per week. Prerequisite: RUS 102 , or three years of successful completion of high school Russian, or demonstrated experiential learning, or by placement test, or equivalent.
courses.description: Continues to develop cultural awareness, listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills, and introduces complex sentence structures. Classes may be conducted in target language. Part I of II. This is a UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Intermediate Russian II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4 hours. Total 4 hours per week. Prerequisite: RUS 201 , or four years of successful completion of high school Russian, or demonstrated experiential learning, or by placement test, or equivalent.
courses.description: Continues to develop cultural awareness, listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills, and emphasizes complex sentence structures. Classes may be conducted in the target language. Part II of II. This is a UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Motorcycle Rider Safety - Beginner
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Laboratory 1-2 hours. Total 2-3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies principles and basic skills of motorcycle riding with an emphasis on safety. Includes street strategies, protective gear, and selection and care/maintenance of motorcycles.

courses.title: Safety & Health Standards: Regulations and Codes
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches development of safety standards, the Occupational Safety and Health Act (OSHA), its rules and regulations; penalties for non-compliance, and methods of compliance. Includes an examination of Government Regulatory Codes and appraisal of consensus, advisory, and proprietary standards.

courses.title: Principles of Industrial Safety
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches principles and practices of accident prevention, analysis of accident causes, mechanical safeguards, fire prevention, housekeeping, occupational diseases, first aid, safety organization, protection equipment and general safety principles and promotion.

courses.title: Industrial Safety
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides basic understanding of safety and health in an industrial situation. Includes hazardous materials, substances, conditions, activities and habits as well as the prescribed methods and equipment needed for the apprentice to protect himself/herself and others.

courses.title: Safety Program Organization and Administration
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces techniques of organizing and administering practical safety programs. Emphasizes safety as a management function. Includes an examination of history, occupational safety and health regulations, and a survey of current laws, codes and standards.

courses.title: Topics In
courses.contact_hours: May be used also for special honors courses. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Provides an opportunity to explore topical areas of interest to or needed by students.

courses.title: Supervised Study
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Assigns problems for independent study incorporating previous instruction and supervised by the instructor.

courses.title: Human Factors & Safety Psychology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies stresses on the human system, both physiological and psychological, that contribute to the severity of industrial accidents. Includes the interrelationship of industrial medicine and industrial hygiene and a study of the various occupational illnesses.

courses.title: Introduction to Environmental and Science Technology I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the basic sciences which describe our physical environment. Includes the fundamentals of geology, meteorology, physics, chemistry, and biology. Describes basic scientific principles and relates them to natural phenomena and the activities of man. Emphasizes field experiences including techniques and data gathering. Part I of II.

courses.title: Introduction to Environmental and Science Technology II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the basic sciences which describe our physical environment. Includes the fundamentals of geology, meteorology, physics, chemistry, and biology. Describes basic scientific principles and relates them to natural phenomena and the activities of man. Emphasizes field experiences including techniques and data gathering. Part II of II.

courses.title: Seminar and Project
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Requires completion of a project or research report related to the student's occupational objectives and a study of approaches to the selection and pursuit of career opportunities in the field.

courses.title: Supervised Study
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Assigns problems for independent study incorporating previous instruction and supervised by the instructor.

courses.title: Seminar and Project
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Requires completion of a project or research report related to the student's occupational objectives and a study of approaches to the selection and pursuit of career opportunities in the field.

courses.title: College Success Skills
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-3 hours. Total 1-3 hours per week.
courses.description: Assists students in transition to colleges. Provides overviews of college policies, procedures, curricular offerings. Encourages contacts with other students and staff. Assists students toward college success through information regarding effective study habits, career and academic planning, and other college resources available to students. May include English and Math placement testing. Strongly recommended for beginning students. Required for graduation.

courses.title: Orientation To (Specify the Discipline)
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-3 hours. Total 1-3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces students to the skills which are necessary to achieve their academic goals, to services offered at the college and to the discipline in which they are enrolled. Covers topics such as services at the college including the learning resources center; counseling, and advising; listening, test taking, and study skills; and topical areas which are applicable to their particular discipline or background.

courses.title: Study Skills
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-3 hours per week.
courses.description: Assists students in planning strategies to overcome nonproductive study habits and in implementing positive study behaviors. Includes management, memory improvement, note taking, and test taking.

courses.title: Preparation for Employment
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides experience in resume writing, preparation of applications, letters of application, and successfully preparing for and completing the job interview. Assists students in identifying their marketable skills and aptitudes. Develops strategies for successful employment search. Assists students in understanding effective human relations techniques and communication skills in job search.

courses.title: Career Education
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-3 hours per week.
courses.description: Surveys career options available to students. Stresses career development and assists in the understanding of self in the world of work. Assists students in applying decision-making to career choice.

courses.title: Seminar and Project
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Requires completion of a project or research report related to the student's occupational objectives and a study of approaches to the selection and pursuit of career opportunities in the field.

courses.title: Supervised Study
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Assigns problems for independent study incorporating previous instruction and supervised by the instructor.

courses.title: Introduction to Sociology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the fundamental concepts and principles of sociology with attention to sociological theory, research methods, and the impact of social inequality. Examines a variety of topics such as culture, race, social class, gender, major social institutions and their role in contemporary society, and the processes of social change. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Cultural Anthropology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines the origins, development, research, diversification and evolution of human cultures. Includes exposure to the variability of both Western and Non-Western aspects of culture. Provides an introduction to the nature of culture and its relationship to various social institutions and societies. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Sociology of the Family
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces tools to study family life through the sociological lens. Explores a variety of topics including various familial forms, divorce, and domestic violence.

courses.title: Family Violence
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines occasions and reasons family relationships do not work. Includes types of family violence, and its prevention.

courses.title: Sociology of Gender
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours, Total 3 hours per week Prerequisite: Ability to read in English at the college level.
courses.description: Analyzes influence of major social institutions and socialization in shaping and changing sex roles in contemporary society. Examines differential access to positions of public power and authority for men and women.

courses.title: Human Sexuality
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies sociological research and theory on sexuality. Includes anatomy and physiology, birth control, sexually transmitted diseases and sexual behavior. Also approved for offering as HLT 136 .

courses.title: Juvenile Delinquency
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies demographic trends, casual theories, and control of juvenile delinquency. Presents juveniles' interaction with family, schools, police, courts, treatment programs, and facilities. Also approved for ADJ Juvenile curriculum.

courses.title: Criminology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies research and causal theories of criminal behavior. Examines crime statistics, crime victims, and types of criminal offenses. Introduces role of police, judicial and correctional system in treatment and punishment of offenders. Is also approved for ADJ Criminology.

courses.title: Sociology of Aging
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces study of aging with special emphasis on later stages of the life cycle. Includes theories of aging, historical and comparative settings, social policy, and future trends of aging.

courses.title: Death and Dying
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: divisional approval.
courses.description: Studies theoretical, practical, and historical aspects of death. Focuses upon student's own ideas, feeling, and attitudes toward death and dying and the significance and consequences of those attitudes.

courses.title: Race and Ethnicity
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Considers race and ethnicity as social constructs that deeply affect personal experience and social institutions. Examines the relationships of racial and ethnic groups with each other and with larger society including ideas of racial inequality both individually and systemically. Introduces significant theoretical approaches to the study of race and ethnicity.

courses.title: Social Problems
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the fundamental concepts underlying social problems construction with attention to how these problems are defined, understood and arbitrated. Examines a variety of topics such as researching social problems and policymaking. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Beginning Spanish I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces cultural awareness, listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills, and emphasizes basic sentence structure. Part I of II. This is a UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Beginning Spanish II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4 hours. Total 4 hours per week. Prerequisite: SPA 101 , or two years of successful completion of high school Spanish, or demonstrated experiential learning, or by placement test, or equivalent.
courses.description: Introduces cultural awareness, listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills and emphasizes basic sentence structure. Part II of II. This is a UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Conversation in Spanish I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: SPA 102 .
courses.description: Emphasizes the spoken language, stressing fluency and correctness of structure, pronunciation, and vocabulary. Part I of II.

courses.title: Conversation in Spanish II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: SPA 102 .
courses.description: Emphasizes the spoken language, stressing fluency and correctness of structure, pronunciation, and vocabulary. Part II of II.

courses.title: Spanish for Health Professionals I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces Spanish to those in the health sciences. Emphasizes oral communication and practical medical vocabulary. May include oral drill and practice. Part I of II.

courses.title: Intermediate Spanish
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: SPA 102 , or three years of successful completion of high school Spanish, or demonstrated experiential learning, or by placement test, or equivalent.
courses.description: Continues to develop cultural awareness, listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills, and introduces complex sentence structures. Classes may be conducted in target language. Part I of II. This is a UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Intermediate Spanish II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: SPA 201 , or four years of successful completion of high school Spanish, or demonstrated experiential learning, or by placement test, or equivalent.
courses.description: Continues to develop cultural awareness, listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills, and emphasizes complex sentence structures. Classes may be conducted in the target language. Part II of II. This is a UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Intermediate Spanish I-II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week. Prerequisite: SPA 102 or equivalent.
courses.description: Continues to develop understanding, speaking, reading, and writing skills. Classes conducted in Spanish. May include oral drill and practice. Part I of II.

courses.title: Intermediate Spanish I-II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week. Prerequisite: SPA 102 or equivalent.
courses.description: Continues to develop understanding, speaking, reading, and writing skills. Classes conducted in Spanish. May include oral drill and practice. Part II of II.

courses.title: Intermediate Conversation I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: SPA 202 or assessment by instructor.
courses.description: Continues to develop fluency through emphasis on idioms and other complex sentence structures. Part I of II.

courses.title: Intermediate Conversation II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: SPA 211 or assessment by instructor.
courses.description: Continues to develop fluency through emphasis on idioms and other complex sentence structures. Part II of II.

courses.title: Introduction to Spanish Civilization & Literature I-II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week. Prerequisite: SPA 202 or equivalent.
courses.description: Introduces the student to Spanish culture and literature. Readings and discussions conducted in Spanish. Part I of II.

courses.title: Introduction to the Travel Industry
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents an overview of the structure and scope of the travel industry with emphasis on job categories and functions, basic vocabulary, and the interrelationships of the various components. Includes the study of information displays of airline computer reservation system.

courses.title: Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems (sUAS) Remote Pilot Ground School
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Total 2-3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents the aeronautical knowledge required for FAA approved commercial operations as a Remote Pilot with small Unmanned Aircraft Systems (sUAS) rating. Covers the regulations applicable to small UAS operations, loading and performance, emergency procedures, crew resource management, determining the performance of the small unmanned aircraft, and maintenance/inspection procedures. Prepares students for the FAA written examination required to obtain the Remote Pilot certificate.

courses.title: Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems (sUAS) Components and Maintenance
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total hours per week 4-5.
courses.description: Provides an introduction to the basic equipment and techniques used in maintaining, repairing, and upgrading sUAS to assure airworthiness and proper operation of the other components. Emphasizes safe practices in repair and handling of components and develops fundamental skills in troubleshooting/repair of the circuits, subsystems and components typically found in the complete sUAS. Covers payload sensor mounting, power management and security threat management.

courses.title: Fundamentals of Welding
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3-6 hours. Total 5-8 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces arc and oxyfuel welding and cutting. Provides fundamental principles of joining ferrous and non-ferrous metals, welding and cutting processes, equipment operation, and safety procedures with emphasis upon welding and cutting procedures.

courses.title: Welding Processes
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces types of welding, their advantages and disadvantages. Points out effects of welds on metals to be machined. Provides practice and demonstration in welding.

courses.title: Arc and Gas Welding
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents arc and gas welding practices. Discusses safety, general welding practices and effects of welding on metals.

courses.title: Welding I (Oxyacetylene)
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches oxygen/acetylene welding and cutting including safety of equipment, welding, brazing and soldering procedures and cutting procedures.

courses.title: Oxyfuel Welding and Cutting
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3-6 hours. Total 5-8 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces history of oxyacetylene welding, principles of welding and cutting, nomenclature of the equipment, development of the puddle, running flat beads, and butt welding in different positions. Explains silver brazing, silver and soft soldering, and safety procedures in the use of tools and equipment.

courses.title: Introduction to Welding
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 3-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces history of welding processes. Covers types of equipment, and assembly of units. Stresses welding procedures such as fusion, non-fusion, and cutting oxyacetylene. Introduces arc welding and plasma arc cutting. Emphasizes procedures in the use of tools and equipment.

courses.title: Arc Welding
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies the operation of AC and DC power sources, weld heat, polarities, and electrodes for use in joining various alloys by the SMAW process. Covers welds in different types of joints and different welding positions. Emphasizes safety procedures.

courses.title: Welding II (Electric Arc)
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 4-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches electric arc welding, including types of equipment, selection of electrodes, safety equipment and procedures, and principles and practices of welding.

courses.title: Shielded Metal Arc Welding (Basic)
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3-6 hours. Total 5-8 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches operation of AC and DC power sources, welding polarities, heats and electrodes for use in joining various metal alloys by the arc welding process. Deals with running beads, butt, and fillet welds in all positions. Emphasizes safety procedures.

courses.title: Shielded Metal Arc Welding (Advanced)
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3-6 hours. Total 5-8 hours per week.
courses.description: Continues instruction on operation of AC and DC power sources, welding polarities, heats and electrodes for use in joining various metal alloys by the arc welding process. Deals with running beads, butt, and fillet welds in all positions. Emphasizes safety procedures.

courses.title: Pipe Welding I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches metal arc welding processes including the welding of pressure piping in the horizontal, vertical, and horizontal-fixed positions in accordance with section IX of the ASME code.

courses.title: Pipe Welding II
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 9 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides practice in the welding of pressure piping in the horizontal, vertical, and fixed positions.

courses.title: Inert Gas Welding
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3-6 hours. Total 5-8 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces practical operations in the uses of inert-gas- shield arc welding. Discusses equipment, safety operations, welding practice in the various positions, process applications, and manual and semi-automatic welding.

courses.title: Inert Gas Welding
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces practical operations in use of inert gas shielded arc welding. Studies equipment operation, setup, safety and practice of GMAW (MIG) and GTAW (TIG).

courses.title: Welding III (Inert Gas)
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies Tungsten and metallic inert gas procedures and practices including principles of operation, shielding gasses, filler rods, process variations and applications, manual and automatic welding, equipment and safety.

courses.title: Welder Qualification Tests I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3-6 hours. Total 5-8 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies techniques and practices of testing welded joints through destructive and non-destructive testing. Part I of II.

courses.title: Welder Qualification Tests II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3-6 hours. Total 5-8 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies techniques and practices of testing welded joints through destructive and non-destructive testing. Part II of II.

courses.title: Welding Metallurgy
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 1-2 hours. Total 3-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies steel classifications, heat treatment procedures, properties of ferrous and non-ferrous metals. Discusses techniques and practices of testing welded joints and destructive/nondestructive, visual magnetic and fluorescent testing.

courses.title: Welding Drawing and Interpretation
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches fundamentals required for successful drafting as applied to the welding industry. Includes blueprint reading, geometric principles of drafting and freehand sketching, basic principles of orthographic projection, preparation of drawings and interpretation of symbols.

courses.title: Gas Metal Arc Welding
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3-6 hours. Total 5-8 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces semi-automatic welding processes with emphasis on practical application. Includes the study of filler wires, fluxes, and gases.

courses.title: Robotic Welding I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour, Laboratory 3 hours, Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines safety, setup, programming, and operation of a welding robot. Covers variables and problems in addition to solutions applied to provide a practical and efficient application of the Gas Metal Arc Welding (GMAW) process to an automated system. (Part I of II)

courses.title: Robotics Welding II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour, Laboratory 3 hours, Total 4 hours per week. Prerequisite: WEL 241
courses.description: Incorporates skills learned in Robotic Welding I into simulating projects used in industry. Focuses on Gas Metal Arc Welding (GMAW) processes used to create weldments taken from industry drawings and blueprints. (Part II of II)

courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3-12 hours. Total 5-14 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces practical operations in use of tungsten arc welding and equipment, operations, safety practices in various positions, shielding gases, filler rods, process variations, and their applications.

courses.description: Introduces practical operations in use of gas metal arc welding and equipment, operations safety practices in various positions, shielding gases, filler rods, process variations, and their applications.
